Service accounts
A Remote Access Service Account enables you to use the Remote Access API to authenticate to Remote Access and access data.
When you create a service account, you can configure it to authenticate using either a private key or a client ID and secret.
If you choose Private Key Signing, a new public/private key pair is generated and downloaded to your machine. This is the only copy of the private key. You are responsible for storing the private key securely. Note its location and ensure the key is accessible to your application; it needs the key to make authenticated API calls.
If you choose Client ID & Secret, authentication is handled using a client secret instead of a private key, allowing integration with services that require this method, such as CyberArk Identity Flows.
Create a service account
-
In the Remote Access portal, go to Identities > Service accounts.
-
Click Create Service Account to display the Create Service Account form, and set the service account properties.
Property
Description
Name
The name of the service account. This name appears in the activities performed with this account.
Description
A description of the service account. This appears in the service accounts list.
Role
Choose a role for the service account that defines its permissions.
- Administrator: can perform all actions and view all tenant information.
- Auditor: can only perform GET actions on 'Activities'.
- Viewer: can perform GET actions on all tenant information, but not create/modify.
Service Account auth type
Select one of the following options:
-
Private Key Signing (default)
-
Client ID & Secret
Both Private Key Signing and Client ID & Secret use the OAuth 2.0 framework. 'Private Key Signing' authenticates with a private key (private_key_jwt), while 'Client ID & Secret' authenticates with a client secret (client_secret_jwt).
The client_secret_jwt method allows integration with CyberArk Identity Flows and other services that require this type of authentication, rather than private key-based authentication.
Status
The status of the new service account.
Confirmation
Select the check box to confirm that you want to create a service account.
-
Click Create Service Account to create the .json file that is required to make the API calls, and save it on your computer. The .json file contains the following:
-
Service Account ID
-
Private key
-
DiscoveryURL
The following example shows the contents of the .json file.
{ "serviceAccountId": "11ea6140f94d5f82a3712de9ac6f6b24", "privateKey": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----------END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----", "discoveryURI": "https://auth.alero.io/auth/realms/serviceaccounts/.well-known/openid-configuration" }
-
Create a JSON Web Token (JWT)
After you create the .json file in the Remote Access portal, and you have the Service Account ID and private key, do the following:
-
Create a JSON Web Token (JWT). There are two ways to create a token; using the API token helper, or you can manually create the token.
-
Call APIs using the Access Token received from the Authorization Server.
Remote Access authenticates clients with a Private Key JWT Client Authentication method (private_key_jwt), which is defined in OpenID Connect 1.0 and the JWT Profile for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication specifications. This is an authentication method that can be used by clients to authenticate to the authorization server when using the token endpoint. Only clients that have registered a public key in the Remote Access portal (by creating a service account) and have signed a JWT using a matching private key (in the file downloaded when creating a Service Account) can authenticate.
When Remote Access authenticates clients with Private Key JWT Client Authentication, the clients send a request that contains an assertion in JWT format to the token endpoint of the server. Remote Access validates the signature and the payload of the assertion.
Recommendation: Although your application can complete these tasks by interacting directly with OAuth 2.0 using HTTP, server-to-server authentication interactions require applications to create and cryptographically sign JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). It is highly recommended to avoid any impact on the security of your application by using using libraries that abstract the cryptography away from your application code.

-
The JAR file you downloaded from CyberArk Marketplace.
-
-t <tenant ID> - Enter your tenant ID value.
-
-p <path-to-secret-file> - Enter the service account secret file path that you received when you created your service account.
-
-
After you run the command, look at the output for the access token.
-
Copy and paste the token to the authorization header value in your request.

Deploy PSM Health Check (ISPSS)
This topic describes how to deploy and configure PSM Health Check.
Typically, load balancers verify PSM server availability by examining network connectivity to the server alone. The PSM Health Check enables you to determine PSM service availability (health) by querying a dedicated PSM Web Service deployed on each PSM instance.
The PSM Web Service verifies PSM service health of the PSM instance upon request and sends a response to the load balancer.
Prerequisites
-
PSM service installed on Windows 2016, Windows 2019, or Windows 2022
-
Web Server (IIS) role is installed
-
The web server is defined with a site binding that is configured to HTTPs using a valid SSL certificate.
Learn how to configure the web server site binding-
In IISP Manager > Actions, select Edit Site > Bindings...
-
In the Site Bindings window, click Edit.
-
In the Edit Site Binding window, enter the details for your SSL certificate:
-
Host name
-
SSL certificate
and click OK.
-
-
Install PSM Health Check
Use a user with administrative privileges to perform this procedure.
To install the Health Check:
-
Install Microsoft .NET Core Windows Server Hosting by downloading the latest Windows hosting bundle:
Go to MicroSoft .Net site: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0 and download ASP.NET Core Runtime 8.0.[latest version] for Windows>Hosting Bundle.
Ensure you follow Microsoft security updates and always use the latest, most up-to-date version.
-
Download the PSM Health Check zip file from the CyberArk Marketplace.
-
Unzip the file.
-
Open an elevated PowerShell window by right-clicking the PowerShell icon and selecting Run as administrator.
-
In the elevated PowerShell window, navigate to the HealthCheck folder.
-
To start the script, run the following command:
./HealthCheck.ps1
To install PSM health check in a non-default location, run the following command:
./HealthCheck.ps1 -installPath <PSM folder non-default path >
For example:
./HealthCheck.ps1 -installPath "F:\Program Files (x86)\Cyberark\PSM"
Configure the response mode
You can configure the response mode of the health check web service.
To configure the response mode:
-
Open the following file:
C:\Program Files (x86)\CyberArk\PSM\HealthCheck\appsettings.json
-
Modify the ResponseMode as follows:
Response Mode
Description
Classic
The health check service responds with 200 (OK) whether the PSM service is healthy or not, but the response body includes PASS or FAIL indicating if the server is healthy.
CodeBased
The health check service responds with 200 (OK) when the PSM service is healthy, and 503(Service unavailable) when the service is not healthy.
HeaderBased
This mode behaves like the Classic mode, but adds a parameter in the response header called IsHealthy, with a value of either Yes or No.
-
Restart the IIS service.
Upgrade PSM Health Check
To upgrade, uninstall any existing .NET core programs and then upgrade PSM Health Check.
Step 1: Uninstall .NET Core
|
Before uninstalling, verify that there are no other programs installed on the PSM server that require .Net Core runtime. |
Go to Control Panel > Programs and Features and uninstall the following programs:
- Microsoft .NET Core <version> - Windows Server Hosting
- Microsoft .NET Core Runtime - <version> (x64)
- Microsoft .NET Core Runtime - <version> (x86)
Step 2: Upgrade PSM Health Check
-
Install Microsoft .NET Core Windows Server Hosting by downloading the latest Windows hosting bundle from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0.
-
Download the PSM Health Check zip file from the CyberArk Marketplace.
-
Unzip the file.
-
In a PowerShell window, navigate to the HealthCheck folder.
-
To start the script, run the following command:
./HealthCheck.ps1 -scriptMode Upgrade
To upgrade PSM health check in a non-default location, run the following command:
./HealthCheck.ps1 -scriptMode Upgrade -installPath <PSM folder non-default path>
Troubleshooting
There are two ways to test the Health Check service:
-
Navigate to: https://<server>/psm/api/health to test if the service is up and running.
-
Run the following PowerShell command, for example: Invoke-WebRequest -uri https://<PSM-SERVER-FQDN>/psm/api/health
If the Health Check service fails, the response code 500 (Internal server error) is returned.
For additional error details, see the PSMWebService.log file located under the HealthCheck folder, by default:
C:\Program Files (x86)\CyberArk\PSM\HealthCheck.

Configure CyberArk Identity SSO integration
This topic describes how to configure Remote Access integration with CyberArk Identity.
Overview
Users with this integration can utilize CyberArk Identity's authentication management features to reach privileged targets protected inside the CyberArk Vault, PVWA, and other elements of PAM - Self-Hosted.
On the Sites page, the sites that can be accessed through CyberArk Identity are marked with the CyberArk Identity icon.
Before you start
Contact your CyberArk account representative to enable Remote Access integration with CyberArk Identity. For details, see the CyberArk Identity documentation.
Before you begin
Before you can configure integration with CyberArk Identity, make sure your system meets the following requirements:
-
Upgrade all the Remote Access connectors in your system to at least 1.0.8901. For details, see Upgrade connectors.
-
Deactivate any other external IdP integrations.
Configure CyberArk Identity integration
Starting April 20, 2025, new Remote Access tenants will have this integration automatically pre-configured. If you want to use CyberArk Identity as your user management source, you can click Apply and skip the steps below.

This section describes how to onboard and manage database targets for access using zero standing privileges (ZSP).
Before you begin
-
SIA does not support TLS termination. To allow connection from client machines to the SIA gateway, make sure you exclude the DNS records of the SIA gateway from your firewall rules.
Ensure the network requirements for connector host, client, and target machines are met. For more information, see Network requirements.
The following database versions are supported:
-
Db2 11.5.0.0 and later
-
MariaDB - 10.0.0 and later
-
MongoDB - 4.0 and later
-
MySQL - 5.7.0 and later
-
Oracle - 18c and later

-

The following is an outline of the workflow to enable access to databases using SIA and zero standing privileges.

If you want to enable connection to Oracle databases, ensure SIA > Settings > Authentication > MFA caching is turned on for databases. The default setting is on.

To onboard a database target:

At Location, select the database location. For example, on-premises or AWS.

Strong account for MariaDB
There are two options for the strong account, based on the authentication method you select for the target:
Use a local strong account to create ephemeral local users
SIA uses a local strong account with permissions to create ephemeral local users and join them to local roles in the database.Each such strong account must have both of the following:
The CREATE USER grant
You can do this with the following query:
GRANT CREATE USER ON *.* TO stronguser WITH GRANT OPTION;
GRANT DROP USER ON *.* TO stronguser WITH GRANT OPTION;
Permissions to alter and manage roles
You can do this with the following query:
GRANT ROLE_ADMIN ON *.* TO stronguser;
Running GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES can also achieve the necessary configuration of the strong account, but it is less secure and we do not recommend it.
For more information, see Manage strong accounts for database targets.
Use an AWS access key to create ephemeral credentials for an RDS IAM user
With this option, SIA uses an AWS access key with permissions to create ephemeral credentials for an RDS IAM user on the target database.

Make sure the target RDS database is configured to use IAM user authentication.
Create a new IAM user or use an existing one.
Make sure this user has rds-db:connect permissions for your desired resources, such as RDS databases and DB users.
Generate an access key and a secret access key. Store these as a strong account in Privilege Cloud, using the Amazon Web Services - AWS - Access Keys platform or in SIA, using RDS IAM user as the secret type.
For more information, see the AWS docs.

Oracle-
Connections using Oracle Real Application Clusters (RAC) via the SCAN listener redirection are not supported. Instead, you must connect directly to the target database node using its associated Virtual IP (VIP) or direct physical IP address.
Connections through a VIP fail certificate validation if the target FQDN or IP address is not listed in the certificate’s Subject Alternative Name (SAN), causing a mismatch during validation.
-
Connections to Oracle databases configured with Native Network Encryption (NNE) are not supported and will fail.
To connect via SIA, ensure that NNE is disabled in the sqlnet.ora configuration file and verify that the following NNE fields are set as follows:
-
SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_SERVER=ACCEPTED
-
SQLNET.CRYPTO_CHECKSUM_SERVER=ACCEPTED
-
SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_CLIENT=ACCEPTED
-
SQLNET.CRYPTO_CHECKSUM_CLIENT=ACCEPTED
-
-
TCPS (TCP\IP with SSL) is a TLS based connection between the proxy or connector and the target database. SIA requires Oracle database targets to be configured with TCPS to provide a fully secure connection.
-
Pay particular attention to the prerequisite mentioned at Strong account details to ensure that the role Secure Infrastructure Privilege Cloud Ephemeral Access has been added to the safe in Privilege Cloud.

SIA for databases uses the Oracle Wallet. For more information, see Oracle Wallet.

SIA uses a strong account with enough permissions to create ephemeral domain users or ephemeral local users and join them to roles in the database. When onboarding the database for access, you can choose whether to authenticate via an ephemeral domain user or a ephemeral local user in the database.
The strong account is based on one of the following authentication methods you select for the target:
Authenticate via an ephemeral domain userIf you choose to authenticate via an ephemeral domain user:
-
You can create an ephemeral domain user and join the user to a group with enough permissions such as Domain Admins, or use Delegate Control to give the user the following permissions:
-
Create, delete, and manage user accounts
-
Modify the membership of a group
For more information, see AD permissions.
-
-
You must also map to the SQL Server database the groups that the ephemeral domain user will be joined to. You can do this manually in SSMS or any other client, or via a set of queries as follows:
-
Create a new login for the AD group using the following command:
CREATE LOGIN <Domain\ADGroupName> FROM WINDOWS;
-
Create a user in the specific database you wish to give permissions to, mapped to the login you created in the preceding step:
USE <YourDatabaseName>
CREATE USER <Domain\ADGroupName> FOR LOGIN <Domain\ADGroupName>;
-
Give permissions to the AD group:
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON <YourTableName> TO <Domain\ADGroupName>;
-
As this is an ephemeral domain user, to follow the least privilege principle, you must make sure the AD groups are restricted to only SQL Server databases.

-
Global roles: manage permissions affecting the entire SQL Server instance. The roles apply to the entire server and are used to control actions that affect the whole server or multiple databases.
-
Database-level roles: manage permissions within a specific database. The roles are used to control access and actions at the database level.
If you choose to authenticate via an ephemeral local user in an SQL Server database, you may create a local strong user and grant it the permissions to create users in the database and join them to roles there by running the following queries.

Use the following to create a new login for the strong account and give the account the permissions required to alter login to roles and groups:
CREATE LOGIN [SIAStrongUser] WITH PASSWORD = '';
USE [master];
GRANT ALTER ANY LOGIN TO [SIAStrongUser];
-
Use the following to create a user in the specific databases you wish to give the permissions required to create users in the database and add users to roles:
USE [TargetDatabase];
CREATE USER [SIAStrongUser] FOR LOGIN [SIAStrongUser];
--- Either grant permissions specifically:
GRANT ALTER ANY USER TO [SIAStrongUser];
GRANT ALTER ROLE TO [SIAStrongUser];
--- Or add user as a db_owner:
EXEC sp_addrolemember db_owner, [SIAStrongUser];
-
Zero standing privileges (ZSP) access to Azure SQL databases is supported only for an SQL Server instance. Setting permissions and access to a specific database within an instance is not supported.

You must define the strong account's username in a User Principal Name (UPN) format. For example, username@azureServerName.

ZSP access is supported only for ephemeral local users. Ephemeral domain users are not supported.
If you choose to authenticate via an ephemeral local user in an Azure SQL database, you can create a local strong user and grant it the permissions to create users in the database and join them to roles there by running the following query.
CREATE LOGIN [SIAStrongUser] WITH PASSWORD = '';
CREATE USER [SIAStrongUser] FOR LOGIN [SIAStrongUser];
GRANT ALTER ANY USER TO [SIAStrongUser];
ZSP access to Azure SQL databases is supported only for ephemeral local users. Ephemeral domain users are not supported.

Set up Windows ZSP access with an ephemeral domain user
This topic describes how to configure an ephemeral domain user to enable zero standing privileges (ZSP) access to Windows targets, as an alternative to an ephemeral local user.
SIA enables a user to access an on-premises or cloud-based Windows target, with zero standing privileges, as an ephemeral local user deleted at the end of the session. Although creating an ephemeral local user provides security advantages, it does not cover all use cases. For example, an ephemeral local user cannot perform domain activities and does not have access to domain resources. You can also configure access to on-premises or cloud-based Windows targets with zero standing privileges via an ephemeral domain user.
You can explicitly configure the Active Directory organizational unit (OU) where the ephemeral domain user is created. If you do not specify an OU, SIA creates the ephemeral domain user in the most common OU of the groups defined in the applied access policy. This setting is available in the Ephemeral domain user location (optional) setting when you enable ephemeral domain user creation, as described in Add a strong account for a Windows target.
The authentication method for ephemeral domain users is determined by the Kerberos authentication setting. For more information, see Authentication settings.
Before you begin
The following steps describe what you must do before doing setting up target access with an ephemeral domain user.
-
Ensure the domain controller machine and the target machines are covered by the same connector pool. This is because SIA uses the target's connector pool to connect to the domain controller machine. For more information, see Manage connector pools and connectors.
-
Ensure that your network is configured as described in Zero standing privileges using Active Directory.
SIA does not require Remote Desktop Services (RDS) Client Access Licenses (CALs) to function. However, if your environment includes Windows servers configured as RDS hosts, they might already use RDS CALs.
If those Windows targets require RDS licensing and are configured to use Per User CALs, each ephemeral domain user who connects consumes one license. To avoid this, the RDS Per Device CALs licensing model is required when connecting with an ephemeral domain user.
You must consider possible resource limitations, such as security identifiers (SIDs), on your domain. Ensure that you have defined proper security controls and alerts to identify anomalies in the number of resources created and deleted in the domain.
Set up target access with an ephemeral domain user
The following steps describe what you must do to enable a user to access on-premises or cloud-based Windows targets with zero standing privileges via an ephemeral domain user.
-
Set up a strong account that is configured to enable creation of ephemeral domain users. For more information, see Add a strong account for a Windows target.
The strong account should be a domain user defined with only the permissions required to perform the following operations in the organizational unit (OU) where ephemeral domain users are created:
-
Create, delete, and manage user accounts
-
Modify the membership of a group
To perform profile cleanup at the end of the session, the account should also have sufficient permissions to delete folders under c:\users on the target servers.
For least privilege considerations, we strongly recommend using an account that has delegation control only on the most common organization unit of the groups defined in the access policy. We do not recommend adding the account to groups, such as Domain Admins, which can provide the expected permissions.
-
-
Set up an access policy and ensure the profile of the access rule is configured to use an ephemeral domain user and add the Active Directory groups that the user will be joined to. For more information, see Create a recurring access policy.
-
At least one group must have permission to remotely access the target. By default, the ephemeral domain user is created in the most common organizational unit (OU) of the groups defined in the access policy.
-
You can explicitly configure the Active Directory organizational unit (OU) where the ephemeral domain user is created. If you do not specify an OU, SIA creates the ephemeral domain user in the most common OU of the groups defined in the applied access policy. This setting is available in the Ephemeral domain user location (optional) setting when you enable ephemeral domain user creation.
-
To ensure the minimum permissions required for access, we strongly recommend defining the Active Directory groups with only the permissions required to perform the operations and to access network resources during the session to the target.
-
Security considerations
Target access with an ephemeral domain user has the following security considerations:
-
Using an ephemeral domain user grants greater access and privileges across the domain as compared to a local user. The domain access level is set according to the groups defined in the access policy for the user. Therefore, when implementing this feature, we strongly recommend following security best practices tools and recommendations, such as those used for firewalls, domain separations, and so on.
-
For secure setup, we strongly recommend that you select and enable the secure configuration options that include certificate validation wherever applicable.

Manage account groups
This topic describes how to manage account groups.
What are account groups
Account groups are accounts that share a secret (password or key) and for which secrets are managed together, whether the secret change is scheduled or initiated by a user.
To associate accounts to an account group, all target accounts must be in the same Safe.
Accounts that belong to a group have two platforms assigned to them:
- Target platform. This is the typical platform associated with an account, which includes the CPM plugin that performs the password change on the target machine.
- Group platform. This platform determines when the password is changed and password policy.
|
Account groups can contain an unlimited number of accounts. However, the number of accounts defined in a group affects the time it takes to perform tasks done on account groups. For example, changing the password for a group of 10 accounts equals to 10 X (the time it takes to change one account). Make sure to consider this when deciding on the group size. |
Before you Create an account group you must first Create a group platform.
In account groups that contain one-time or exclusive passwords, all the members of the group are changed automatically after the one-time password has been used or after an exclusive password has been checked in. For details, see Manage exclusive accounts groups and Manage one-time accounts in groups.
Create a group platform

Manage exclusive accounts groups
All the accounts in exclusive accounts groups are locked when any account in the group is retrieved. Each account can only be retrieved after it has been changed and released.
After this type of group is released, all members of the group will be changed before they are released. From the time when the password change process begins until the last password in the account group has been changed, the group is not fully available. This means that group members that have not yet been changed, cannot be retrieved.
Follow the instructions in Edit a platform and edit the following platform settings to ensure that these accounts are maintained as exclusive accounts in groups:
Property | Description |
|---|---|
UnlockIfFail | In both the group platform and the target platform, set UnlockIfFail to No, to ensure that all the accounts in the group are released only after their passwords have been changed. When set to Yes, if the password change process fails, the account will be unlocked and can be accessed, but it will not be changed. |
ResetOveridesMinValidity ResetOverridesTimeFrame | In the target platform, set ResetOveridesMinValidity and ResetOverridesTimeFrame to Yes, to ensure that accounts are released immediately after they are changed. |
ImmediateInterval | In the group platform, make sure that the value of ImmediateInterval is higher than the value of this property in the target platform. |
MinValidityPeriod | In the target platform, specify the number of minutes between the last time that an account was retrieved and when the entire group is replaced. |
Manage one-time accounts in groups
When a one-time account in a group is retrieved, the group isn’t locked and all other members are still available for other users. However, after the time specified in the MinValidityPeriod elapses, all the passwords in the entire group of accounts are changed.
In the target platform, follow the instructions in Edit a platform and edit MinValidityPeriod to specify the number of minutes between the last time that an account was retrieved and when the entire group is replaced.

Exceptions
After setting a Master Policy that determines how accounts will be managed in the entire organization, you can create exceptions to add granularity as needed and set different behavior for specific platforms that will override the corresponding rules set by the Master Policy. Execptions can be set for a scope of accounts associated with a specific platform. The Master Policy, together with the exceptions defined on each platform, determine the resultant behavior of the system on each account, based on its Platform.
To define more granularity for a specific scope of accounts, such as the Windows PCI accounts, after you define the Master Policy, you can duplicate a Windows platform in Platform Management and define an exception that contains specific rules that are relevant to Windows PCI only. The unique combination of the Master Policy rules together with the exception ensures that each platform is managed exactly according to your needs, with minimum configuration.
Initially, when a user adds an exception, it inherits all values from the Master Policy and these values still adopt any changes made in the Master Policy. However, if a user changes the value of any setting in the exception, either basic or advanced, the new value overrides the value that was inherited from the Master Policy and disconnects the setting value from the Master Policy. To emphasize this, a broken chain icon is displayed next to the ‘disconnected’ setting.
In addition, any changes made in a Master Policy after an exception is created do not affect any settings in the exception that override the Master Policy; they only affect the settings in the exception that inherit directly from Master Policy. This is especially relevant when a rule contains several basic and advanced settings, and some of the exception settings may inherit values from the Master Policy and some override it.
For example, an enterprise decides that users can connect directly to target systems (“Click to Connect”) but can still view passwords when needed (i.e. utilize the “Show” or “Copy” functions). However, the Windows PCI accounts cannot be viewed by users and can only be accessed through the ‘Connect’ button. In this case, an exception will be created for the rule that defines that users can connect directly to target systems on a Windows PCI platform. The basic setting remains without changes (meaning that it inherits from the Master Policy), while the advanced setting that determines that users can view passwords will be disabled, overriding the Master Policy.
The following scenario describes a typical workflow using the Master Policy and Platform Management technical settings.
In a large enterprise that manages multiple accounts on local and remote machines, a Risk Manager has issued a security policy defining that all passwords in the organization must be changed every 90 days. In response, the IT/IS Group Manager informed him that passwords for the Windows PCI systems in the organization’s US offices only need to be changed once a year. In addition, the Vault Administrator has suggested using a different port to manage Windows_US PCI systems.
To ensure compliance with enterprise and standard policies, the Compliance Auditor emphasizes the importance of compliancy and wants to know how to verify that all accounts comply with the Master Policy.
The new Master Policy enables all the above users to get what they want:
| ■ | The Master Policy defines password changes for all privileged accounts every 90 days. |
| ■ | An exception is created within the Master Policy to change passwords on Windows PCI systems in the US offices once a year. |
| ■ | The Compliance Auditor can see the effective accounts policy that is enforced throughout the organization in the Master Policy, and can view compliancy to it in the standard compliance report. |
| ■ | Finally, technical settings that are set in the new Platform Management page enable the Vault administrator to set a different port or any other technical settings for all accounts that are managed on the Windows_US PCI system. |

Master Policy in the modern interface
The Master Policy enables you to define a baseline for how you manage accounts in your organization. You can define and view these rules on the Platform Management page in the modern interface. The rules are shown at the top of the page.
Master Policy rules
You can set Master Policy rules for access workflows, password management, session management, and audit. Click Master policy > Edit master policy to edit the rules.
You cannot create exceptions to the Master Policy rules. Exceptions must be created in the classic interface. For details, see Exceptions.
Access Workflows
These are the main policy rules and settings that define how your organization manages access to privileged accounts.
Users can check out an account and lock it so that no other users can retrieve it at the same time. After the user has used the password, they check the password back into the Vault. Together with enforcing one-time password access, this restricts access to a single user, ensuring exclusive usage of the privileged account and guaranteeing accountability. By default, this rule is inactive.
For more information, refer to Account check-out and check-in.
Users can only retrieve accounts after they specify a reason. By default, this rule is active.
You can also determine whether users can specify a free text reason in the Reason edit box or must select one of the predefined reasons.
Accounts can be retrieved for one-time use only, and the password stored inside must be changed after each use before the account is released and can be used again. Passwords can be changed automatically by the Privileged Access Manager - Self-Hosted solution’s password management capability. By default, this rule is inactive.
For more information, refer to Account check-out and check-in.
Users must receive approval from authorized users before they can access passwords. This enables you to see who wants to access passwords, when, and for what purpose. By default, this rule is inactive.
You can determine the following workflows:
-
Whether requests for privileged accounts require approval from multiple levels of users.
-
Whether requests for privileged accounts must be approved by a direct manager.
-
The number of authorized users required to confirm requests.
For more information, refer to Dual control.
Determine whether users can view their passwords.
Users can connect to remote devices without needing to know or specify the required password. This prevents the password from being exposed to the user and maintains productivity as the user does not have to open a login session and then copy and paste the password credentials into it. In addition, advanced settings define whether or not users are permitted to view passwords. This enforces strong authentication for accessing managed devices and restricts user access to passwords according to granular access control. By default, this rule is active.
Password Management
These rules determine how passwords are managed.
Passwords will be verified after the timeframe specified in the previous rule. They can be changed manually or replaced by a unique and highly secure password that is randomly generated by the Password Vault. By default, passwords are verified every 7 days.
The Master Policy determines how frequently passwords must be changed. By default, passwords are changed every 90 days. You can see when password changes are planned in the Compliance Report.
Session Management
These rules determine whether privileged sessions are recorded, and how they are monitored.
All IT administrator privileged sessions on remote machines will be monitored and isolated. By default, this rule is inactive.
All activities in each privileged session in text and/or video format will be recorded and stored in the Vault, compressed, for future auditing. These recordings are transparent to users and cannot be bypassed. By default, this rule is active.
Audit
This rule determines how Safe audits are retained.
This rule controls the number of days that Safe activities audits are retained. By default, audits of activities are kept for 90 days.
If this parameter is set to zero, activities in the Safe are not written to an audit log.

Enable HSTS
HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a policy mechanism that helps to protect websites against man-in-the-middle attacks such as protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking. It allows web servers to declare that web browsers (or other complying user agents) should automatically interact with it using only HTTPS connections.
Follow these steps to enable HSTS on your Windows Server 2019 and later:
-
Open the Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager and click the site that runs your ConfigMgr roles. By default this will be Default Web Site on the left pane.
-
Click HSTS on the right pane.
-
Select Enable and set the Max-Age to 31536000 (1 year). Select IncludeSubDomains and Redirect Http to Https.
Follow these steps to enable HSTS on your Windows Server 2016:
-
Open Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager and select the site your ConfigMgr roles are running from (by default this will be Default Web Site).
-
Double click HTTP Response Headers, then click Add from the Actions pane on the left.
-
In the Name field enter “Strict-Transport-Security”, and in the Value field enter “max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains”.
-
Click OK to save this header.
Configure a hardened server to accept OS user authentication
When hardening a server, all non-administrator users become blocked from authenticating to the hardened server using OS user authentication.
When Central Credential Provider is installed on a hardened PVWA, you need to reconfigure the authenticated users on this server:
- Go to the Local security policy.
- Under User Rights Assignment, select Access this computer from the network.
-
In the policy's properties, add the Authenticated Users group. This allows all non-administrator users to connect to Central Credential Provider using OS user authentication and successfully retrieve secrets.
|
This configuration change allows more users to connect to your PVWA server and, as a result, may expand the attack surface on that server. To control user access on this server, you can add a user-defined group instead of the Authenticated Users group. |

Create the Credential Provider Environment in the Vault / Privilege Cloud for UNIX
If you did not create the Credential Provider environment in the Vault / Privilege Cloud during installation, you can create it manually after installation using the Vault / Privilege Cloud parameter file and CreateCredFile utility that you copied from the installation media to a local folder.
To create a Credential Provider environment manually:
-
Open the Vault.ini file and specify the parameters of the Vault / Privilege Cloud that will be accessed by the Credential Provider.
For more information about the Vault.ini configuration file, refer to Vault.ini.
-
Run the CreateCredFile utility with all the relevant flags set, using the following syntax:
CreateCredFile <FileName> <command> [command parameters]
For more information about creating user credential files, see Credential file usage in Credential Providers (CP).
-
Use an administrative user to create the Credential Provider environment in the Vault / Privilege Cloud.
-
Create the credential file on the machine where it will be used.
-
Creating a credential file on a remote machine and using it for several Credential Provider installations is less secure and is not our recommended best practice.
-
The user credential file must be placed in a folder that is accessible only for the machine or domain administrator who runs the Credential Provider installation. We strongly recommend that you delete the credential file after completing the registration.
-
-
At a command line, run the CreateEnv utility that was copied to the bin folder during Credential Provider installation, using the following syntax:
./createenv -CredFilePath <CredFilePath> -VaultFilePath <VaultFilePath> -AppProviderUser <ProviderUserName> -AppProviderConfSafe <ConfigurationSafeName> -MainAppProviderConfFilePath <MainConfigurationFilePath> -OverrideExistingConfFile <Y\N> -OverrideExistingCredFile <Y\N> -PIMConfigurationSafe <PIMConfigurationSafeName> -AppProviderUserLocation <ApplicationUsersLocation> -LicensedProducts <CP\CP-ZOS>

What's new
New Secure Infrastructure Access (SIA) versions are released and announced on a varying cadence. Occasionally, new versions that include only performance, stability and bug fixes, and do not require customer actions, are released without an announcement.
February 25, 2026

The Secure Access space and Secure Infrastructure Access (SIA) will soon enforce a consistent reason prompt when user access requires justification.
When the Require users to specify a reason for access master policy is enabled in Privilege Cloud, users must manually enter a reason before access is granted. Automatically pre-filled reasons are no longer supported.
This enforcement applies consistently to the following access methods:

Showing passwords in the Secure Access space
-
SIA connections initiated through the Secure Access space (RDP and SSH)
-
Native SIA connections (RDP and SSH)
-
Access through the SIA API (RDP and SSH)
This change captures a clear, user-provided justification, regardless of how users perform access, which improves governance and auditability.

February 9, 2026
Improved performance for Windows RDP connections
Windows RDP connections are now faster and have lower latency. When a session starts, SIA automatically selects the RDP gateway closest to the end user, improving performance, especially when the end user and the tenant are in different geographic regions.
This enhancement introduces temporary caching of relevant data across multiple regions. It supports the ongoing transition to location-aware routing, as previously announced.
This improvement will be gradually released to all regions by the end of February 2026.
For more information, see Data caching for Windows and database target connections.

This enhancement enables administrators to place ephemeral domain users directly in governed, Group Policy Object (GPO)–enforced OUs instead of default containers, improving control and Active Directory hygiene. Support for Windows environments that enforce LDAP server signing and Channel Binding Token
SIA now supports Windows environments that enforce LDAP server signing and Channel Binding Token (CBT).
This support enables SIA to operate in hardened Active Directory (AD) environments where these security controls are required when access is performed for users with zero standing privileges (ZSP) to establish secure RDP sessions to Windows and databases access.
LDAP server signing ensures that all LDAP directory queries, such as retrieving user attributes and group memberships, are integrity-protected and accepted only when signed. This prevents tampering and blocks downgraded or unsigned LDAP communication.
CBT binds authentication to the specific TLS session between SIA and the Windows target. This prevents man-in-the-middle attacks, credential relay, and session proxying for both Kerberos and NTLM authentication.
Together with existing Kerberos authentication support, these controls provide a robustly-secured authentication and authorization for environments aligned with Microsoft’s latest AD security baselines.

July 14, 2025
Action required for change to CyberArk SIA service connectivity
To improve reliability and provide more flexible access for users connecting from different regions, we’re updating how network access to the CyberArk SIA service is managed. This change is part of a broader transition that will enable future enhancements, such as location-aware routing.
What's changing
In the coming weeks, we will only allow connectivity to the CyberArk SIA service through fully qualified domain names (FQDNs). IP-based access for end-user machines will no longer be supported. Connectors can continue to use IP ranges but we strongly recommend using FQDNs.
This change affects:
-
Organizations that use IP addresses for end-user machine connectivity to the CyberArk SIA service.
-
Organizations that use static IP address configurations in the connector host machine’s outbound firewall rules.
If your setup already uses FQDNs, no action is required.
What you need to do
If you're currently using IP addresses, you should update all relevant firewall configurations to allow access only through the specified FQDNs, and ensure that all client machines meet connectivity requirements. For more information, see Client machines.
If your connector host machine uses static IP configurations, you should update outbound firewall rules to support FQDN-based communication, as recommended.
If FQDNs cannot be used, you should configure a range of IP addresses instead. For more information, see Configuration details.
We’re sharing this information in advance to give your teams time to prepare. IP-based connectivity will be deprecated in the coming weeks.
Contact your CyberArk representative for any additional information or questions.

Easy RDP connection to multiple targets by using multi-factor authentication (MFA) caching
The enhanced RDP MFA caching capability enables users to connect to multiple targets using a token that is generated once for all targets, saving the need to perform MFA authentication on every target access.
The Infrastructure page connection guide in the Secure Access space has a new Token tab that enables users to generate the MFA token. Token (MFA caching): Enables access to multiple authorized targets with a cached MFA token, using any RDP client. The token is valid for a configured time period.

CyberArk is expanding its ability to provide secure access to privileged web applications using credentials stored in the CyberArk Vault. This enhancement introduces native access capabilities - enabling users to launch web apps directly from their own browsers using vaulted credentials - while maintaining session protection and recording.

The new name more accurately and clearly communicates the value of Secure Infrastructure Access. The former name is no longer accurate, as the Secure Infrastructure Access component also now supports use of vaulted credentials, in addition to access with zero standing privileges.

We recommend customers and partners update any internal documentation on architecture, deployment and user guides for your PAM program.

Customers: Reach out to your CyberArk account team with any questions or to learn more about the Secure Infrastructure Access component.
Partners: Reach out to your Channel Account Manager with further questions.

Previously, session management through DPA to Windows targets worked by having users connect with a native RDP client and the request directed through the DPA cloud service.
The Remote Desktop Gateway (RD Gateway) is a component that enables the establishment of an RDP connection from the end user to the target, but tunneled through an HTTPS connection. This eliminates the need to allow RDP connections from users to the DPA service through the internet, thus improving the security of the connection.
From March 31, 2024, RD Gateway will be the only entry point for RDP sessions.
Call to action:
-
If you use the Connection guidance page to generate an RDP file for connection, you do not need to take any action other than follow the instructions on the page. The automatically generated RDP file will have additional parameters. For more information, see Connect to a Windows target.
-
If you have a previously generated RDP file and saved it for later use, or if you are using a Connection Manager, you will only be able to connect if you follow the updated instructions. For more information, see Connect to a Windows target.

February 18, 2024
Just-in-time permissions for vaulted credentials
We provide several methods to isolate and monitor privileged sessions while reducing the risks of standing access. The primary objective, in alignment with the CyberArk Blueprint, is to reduce the risk of stolen credentials with standing privileges. One primary method to achieve this objective is provisioning access by creating an ephemeral user with time-bound permissions to access resources tagged with certain attributes (known as attribute-based access control).
We understand that this approach is not suitable for all customers and use cases. For example, a user needs to access targets with a personal privileged domain account that is managed in a vault, but the security admin would like this account to have least privileges and to only be accessible when required, through just-in-time provisioning.
To address customer requirements and feedback, we have expanded the scope of session management with zero standing privileges.
Users can now connect to targets with credentials that are managed in the Privilege Cloud Vault with little or no associated permissions. Upon connecting to a target system, users receive only a selected range of relevant permissions defined in the appropriate policy. At the end of the user’s session, these permissions are removed.
With this new workflow, users can access Windows targets on a just-in-time basis, with time-bound sessions. Security teams can meanwhile maintain the existing user profiles of an account, including key credential management and rotation policies.
This addition builds on our existing capabilities for users to access targets with zero standing privileges without the risk and operational burden of an existing account or credential.
For more information, see Connect to a Windows target.

Introducing Dynamic Privileged Access
We are proud to introduce Dynamic Privileged Access, a new born-in-the-cloud, SaaS-delivered service and part of the Identity Shared Services Platform.
DPA provisions just-in-time access to cloud-hosted virtual machines and on-premise environments, reducing risk and enabling organizations to unlock the operational efficiencies.
DPA was designed to help reduce the risk associated with standing access to the IT estate. For day-to-day operations, administrators, DevOps engineers and business owners experience privileged access exactly when they require it for high-frequency-access use cases. For one-time tasks, support engineers receive ad-hoc, ITSM-ticket-initiated, session-limited, privileged access to highly sensitive infrastructure for the required amount of time.
DPA enables defining “who” can access “what,” based on the organization’s joiner, mover and leaver rapid changes, as well as the lifetime and business context of dynamic Amazon AWS/Microsoft Azure Linux or on-premises Microsoft Windows servers. Stop using static IDs and start leveraging your already-existing attributes like region, network and custom tags for application, project or environment. For the Microsoft Windows on-premises servers, users can query partial or specific Fully Qualified Domain Names (FQDNs).
Utilize the CyberArk access brokering service that enables users to connect to remote private networks without direct inbound connectivity. Enforce strong, adaptive, multi-factor authentication (MFA) for each specific identity based on behavioral analytics, and establish isolated sessions to your Amazon AWS/Microsoft Azure Linux or Microsoft Windows on-premises environments.
DPA provides support for native connectivity, enabling users to continue leveraging preferred RDP or SSH clients of choice, while enforcing modern MFA methods through the use of personal credentials in a native, browserless fashion.
DPA delivers value on day 1 by establishing agentless, non-intrusive connectivity without exposing the organization’s internal network. The solution is seamlessly integrated into CyberArk’s CyberArk Identity Security Platform Shared Services Shared Services, providing unified user management, authentication and component deployment.

Activate offline access for Privilege Cloud accounts
This topic describes how to activate offline access for your Privilege Cloud accounts.
Overview
Using the CyberArk Mobile app, you are able to store certain privileged accounts locally on your mobile device. Cached passwords are stored safely and are available when Privilege Cloud is unavailable, or there is no Remote Access or internet connectivity.
For users or vendors to access offline credentials, you need to activate offline access for each of your tenants.
When a user or vendor is removed from the tenant, all retrieved offline credentials are removed from their mobile device as well.
Offline access is compatible with all Privilege Cloud versions and PAM - Self-Hosted 10.3 and higher.
For optimal performance and load management, we recommend storing no more than 100 accounts per device for offline use.
Prerequisites
-
Users are registered with Remote Access. For more information, see Company user access or Vendor access.
-
Users are registered to CyberArk Mobile. For more information, see Mobile app.
-
Company users are authenticated to their company directory. For more information, see Configure external Identity Provider integration or Configure Active Directory integration.
-
Privilege Cloud tenants support External IdP authentication only.
Limitations
-
Accounts under certain policies cannot be saved offline:
-
Enforced check-in/check-out exclusive access
-
Requires dual control password access approval
-
Enforced one-time password access
-
Ticketing systems integration
-
-
Enforced user login only via IdP is not supported. For more information, see Set enforcement
For accounts that have Dual Control enabled, Offline Access can be used if the user accessing the account has Access without Confirmation permissions in the Safe. For more information, see Enable a Safe owner to access a Safe without confirmation.
Activate offline access
As an administrator, activate offline access for each of your tenants.
-
Log in to the Remote Access Admin portal: https://portal.alero.io/ (change the URL according to your datacenter).
-
Select a tenant. In the Remote Access menu, click Settings > General.
-
In the Offline Access to PAM accounts section, set the following:
Setting
Description
Allow company users to cache account credentials offline to maintain access when PAM is unavailable
Enables users to securely store account credentials on their mobile devices to maintain access when PAM is unavailable.
Allow offline access for vendors Allows external vendors to access stored credentials offline from their mobile devices. Allow access to offline credentials when Remote Access service is unavailable Users can retrieve stored credentials from their mobile devices even when the Remote Access service is down.
No verification against the organization will be performed before granting access.
Allow access to offline credentials when no network connection is available to the CyberArk Mobile app
Enables users to access stored credentials when their mobile device is offline.
No verification against the organization will be performed before granting access.
Unrestricted mode
When enabled, allows company users or vendors to download and view their account password from their mobile device even if all services are available.
This option can be used for testing the availability of your account offline password. Make sure this option is disabled when your tests are completed.
Sync offline credentials
Enable automatic sync
-
When enabled, offline credentials are automatically synchronized at the configured interval without user interaction.
-
When disabled, users need to manually sync the account credentials. You can set the amount of days to send an app reminder to sync offline accounts.
Configure the automatic interval / sync reminder
When automatic sync is enabled, define how often offline credentials are updated to ensure they remain current.
-
Days - Set synchronization in a range of 1 to 365 days.
-
Hours - Choose a more frequent sync interval between 3 and 23 hours.
To ensure automatic sync is enabled, the user must keep the CyberArk Mobile app running in the background.
To do this, make sure the notification settings for the app are as follows:
Android:
Go to Settings > Apps > CyberArk Mobile > Notifications
iOS:
Go to Settings > Notifications > Notification Style > select CyberArk Mobile
When automatic sync is disabled, set the amount of days to send an app reminder to sync offline accounts.
Notify the user if the sync didn't occur for X days
Sends an alert if offline credentials have not been synchronized for the specified number of days.
The number of days must be greater than the sync interval (e.g., if the sync interval is 7 days, the notification threshold must be 8 days or more).
Restrict automatic sync during the following timeframe
Allows administrators to define specific periods when automatic sync should be paused (e.g., to reduce server load during peak hours).
The restriction period aligns with the timezone of the user’s mobile device.
-
- Click Save.
View last offline sync
You can check the last offline sync for each user or vendor from their details page.
In the Remote Access portal, go to Identities > Users / Vendors.
For information about user and vendor access to offline accounts credentials, see Access Privilege Cloud accounts offline credentials.
Restrict offline access per account
As an administrator, you can restrict offline access for specific accounts from the PVWA.
This feature is supported from CyberArk Mobile app version 7.0 and up. Users using previous versions of the CyberArk Mobile app will continue to be able to cache the password of any account they have permissions to access.
-
Download the Restrict Offline Access platform from CyberArk Marketplace.
-
Log in to the PVWA as a user with administrative rights and go to Administration > Platform Management.
-
Click Import platform and select the Restrict Offline Access platform you downloaded.
An optional parameter named DisableforOfflineAccess is added to the account properties.
-
Edit an existing account, or create a new one, and navigate to Account properties.
-
Set the Disable for Offline Access value to True. (Default = False)
Offline access activities
When using offline access, activities are recorded as follows:
-
Marking an account for offline availability - When an account is marked for offline access, it is retrieved and securely stored on the mobile device. This action generates an activity entry in Privilege Cloud to record the retrieval.
-
The synchronization process - During synchronization, an activity entry similar to the one generated when marking an account for offline availability is created.
For details about viewing activities in Privilege Cloud, see Audit action codes.
-
Offline usage - While the device is in offline mode, any usage of offline accounts is logged locally. These offline actions are queued for activity submission and are only sent to Remote Access portal when the CyberArk Mobile app reconnects to online mode.
For details about viewing activities in Remote Access, see Monitor activities

Delete accounts with offboarding rule sets
This topic describes how to create and manage predefined rule sets that automatically delete legacy accounts that are no longer found in your environment.
Automatic analysis and account management helps you to quickly identify and delete legacy accounts that are no longer in use and no longer require privilege management.
Overview
Inactive legacy accounts clutter Privilege Cloud and consume valuable resources.
To avoid the manual analysis and offboarding steps, you can define offboarding rule sets, based on absence criteria and other account properties, to automatically delete inactive legacy accounts.
Offboarding rules use account properties and the Boolean expressions If/Then and ElseIf/Then to identify specific accounts and delete them from Privilege Cloud.
Check the Accounts View list from time to time to check for any inactive legacy account and identify account properties that can be used to define new offboarding rule sets to automatically clean up your Privilege Cloud environment.
If accounts were deleted by offboarding rules and the devices come back online, they will be rediscovered in the next scan.
Choose accounts for running your system rule sets
When you define a new rule set, or edit an existing rule set, this triggers a rerun of all rule sets on your system accounts. At this time you can choose to rerun the system rule sets on either existing accounts or only on future accounts. All system rules are run, including the newly added/edited rule set.
The time required to rerun all rule sets on existing accounts varies, depending on the number of accounts in your system. In systems with a large number of accounts, we recommend to consider rerunning updated rule sets after you have completed all your planned rule set updates.

Master Policy Rules
The Master Policy enables you to define a baseline for how you manage accounts in your organization. You can define and view these rules in the Master Policy page. Click a section title to display the policy rules defined in that section, as well as the status of each rule and possible exceptions to it.
To display this page, users must be members of the Vault Admins group.
Master Policy rules
The Master Policy Page enables you to set Master Policy rules for privileged access workflows, password management, and session management.
Privileged Access Workflows
These are the main policy rules and settings that define how your organization manages access to privileged accounts.
Users must receive approval from authorized users before they can access passwords. This enables you to see who wants to access passwords, when, and for what purpose. By default, this rule is inactive.
Advanced settings enable you to determine the following workflows:
-
Whether requests for privileged accounts require approval from multiple levels of users.
-
Whether requests for privileged accounts must be approved by a direct manager.
-
The number of authorized users required to confirm requests.
For more information, refer to Dual control.
Users can check out an account and lock it so that no other users can retrieve it at the same time. After the user has used the password, they check the password back into the Vault. Together with enforcing one-time password access, this restricts access to a single user, ensuring exclusive usage of the privileged account and guaranteeing accountability. By default, this rule is inactive.
For more information, refer to Account check-out and check-in.
Accounts can be retrieved for one-time use only, and the password stored inside must be changed after each use before the account is released and can be used again. Passwords can be changed automatically by the Privileged Access Manager - Self-Hosted solution’s password management capability. By default, this rule is inactive.
For more information, refer to Account check-out and check-in.
Users can connect to remote devices without needing to know or specify the required password. This prevents the password from being exposed to the user and maintains productivity as the user does not have to open a login session and then copy and paste the password credentials into it. In addition, advanced settings define whether or not users are permitted to view passwords. This enforces strong authentication for accessing managed devices and restricts user access to passwords according to granular access control. By default, this rule is active.
Users can only retrieve accounts after they specify a reason that explains why they want to retrieve them. By default, this rule is active.
An advanced setting determines whether users will be able to specify a free text reason in the Reason edit box or will be required to select one of the predefined reasons.
Password Management
These rules determine how passwords are managed.
The Master Policy determines how frequently passwords must be changed. By default, passwords are changed every 90 days. You can see when password changes are planned in the Compliance Report.
Passwords will be verified after the timeframe specified in the previous rule. They can be changed manually or replaced by a unique and highly secure password that is randomly generated by the Password Vault. By default, passwords are verified every 7 days.
Session Management
These rules determine whether or not privileged sessions are recorded, and how they are monitored.
All IT administrator privileged sessions on remote machines will be monitored and isolated. By default, this rule is inactive.
All activities in each privileged session in text and/or video format will be recorded and stored in the Vault, compressed, for future auditing. These recordings are transparent to users and cannot be bypassed. By default, this rule is active.
Audit
This rule determines how Safe audits are retained.
This rule controls the number of days that Safe activities audits are retained. By default, audits of activities are kept for 90 days.
If this parameter is set to zero, activities in the Safe will not be written in an audit log.

| ■ | Make sure that sensitive data will not be saved to the disk during the session; in case some data is saved, consider cleaning this data as part of the AutoIt script. |
| ■ | PSM provides the ability to block any user interaction that may interfere with the login procedure. When the login procedure of the Universal Connector connection component starts, PSM prevents the user from typing keystrokes or using the mouse until it receives an indication from the SendPID function that the login procedure is completed. Make sure that the SendPID function is called only after the login procedure is completed. For more information, see SendPID. |
If your Universal Connector connection component requires user input during login, you can disable this block by adding the client specific parameter BlockUserInput. For details, see Configure a Custom Universal Connector.

Discover local accounts using EPM
This topic presents the workflow for discovering unmanaged local Windows, macOS, and Linux accounts using the account discovery service. This discovery option is based on EPM scanning of endpoints, including loosely connected devices, which are devices that are not always connected to the network.
EPM agents scan endpoints according to the settings defined in the EPM configuration. The result of each scan is a list of local accounts, including accounts from loosely connected devices. The scans are run periodically and are displayed in Identity Protection under Discovery & Remediations > Discovered identities > Accounts every 24 hours.
Learn more about Local account discovery with CyberArk EPM.
When you deploy an EPM agent on an endpoint machine and it is detected by the set it's connected to, the agent reports its inventory to the EPM service. The inventory sent by endpoint machines that are part of a domain includes a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN). The inventory sent by endpoint machines that are not part of a domain does not include a FQDN.
When an endpoint machine is added to a domain after the EPM agent has sent at least one inventory, that machine might appear twice in Identity Protection, once with details that include FQDN data and another with details that do not include FQDN data.
The FQDN data may appear after the hostname, because it depends on when the agent uploads its full inventory.
Set up the Discovery service
The discovery and EPM tenants must be located in the same AWS region.
-
In the top right corner of the CyberArk screen:
-
Next to your username, expand the drop-down menu and click About.
-
In Tenant details > ID field, click the Copy icon to store the tenant ID string for use in subsequent steps.
-
-
In the EPM Management console:
-
Select the set to configure, then go to Configuration> Set configuration.
-
Select Credentials rotation> Discover local administrators and in More options, click Edit.
-
Toggle Discover local administrators to On.
-
Enter your tenant ID (saved in Step 1) and click Done.
-
In the configuration page, click Save.
-
EPM starts to collect loosely connected devices.

Configuration considerations for Secrets Manager applications with the Vault
This topic describes considerations and best practices to configure Secrets Manager applications such as CP, CCP, and Vault Synchronizer with the Vault to optimize Vault performance and reduce overhead.
Following the best practices below will help to avoid potential performance or stability issues with the Vault.
PAM considerations and best practices
-
Make sure that the PAM and Secrets Manager components have not reached the end of their lifecycle. For more information, see End of Life policy.
-
The PAM and Secrets Manager components must have compatible versions installed. For more information about compatibility, see Supported performance configurations.
-
We recommend that you upgrade the PAM and Secrets Manager components to the latest Long Term Support (LTS) version This includes both the Vault, PVWA and the Secrets Manager components to take advantage of all the performance improvements and bug fixes. For more information about LTS version support levels, see LTS Version Support levels.
-
For each Secrets Manager component, plan the Safes and their access and make sure that you follow the guidelines below:
-
Set the least number possible of required Safes for each Secrets Manager component.
-
Set each Secrets Manager component user so that only this user has access to the Safe. Configuring multiple Secrets Manager component users to the same Safe may lead to performance degradation due to the database locking. This only applies to Secrets Manager component users, not human users.
-
Set each Safe so that it only contains the application accounts that are used by the specific Secrets Manager component.
-
Using workflows such as one-time password or exclusive may impact performance. Use workflows only when necessary.
You can implement this by planning, storing and managing the accounts in Safes where each Safe is assigned to one Secrets Manager component, and the application accounts stored in the Safe are only those that the Secrets Manager component uses.
-
-
Configure the Safe properties using the following guidelines:
-
Do not enable the Object Level Access Control (OLAC) property. If you have enabled OLAC for the Safe, you must create a new Safe and move the accounts to the new Safe.
-
We recommend to select account history retention using versions, setting the value to 2 versions. These two versions are the current version and the previous version.
-
If you want to use account history retention by days, the retention result should not exceed a total of 2-3 versions per account. In order to calculate this accurately, you will need to change the retention value or the CPM policy.
Set the CPM rotation policy so that it is identical for all accounts in a Safe.
If the CPM rotation policy is not identical for all accounts, duplicate the CPM policy and configure the rotation policy for the new Safe configuration. Then, separate the accounts into different Safes according to the CPM rotation policy.
Example 1:
If the CPM rotation policy for all platforms in a Safe is configured to rotate the credentials daily, set the retention to 2 days.
Example 2:
If the CPM rotation policy for all platforms in a Safe is configured to rotate the credentials monthly, set the retention to 60 days.
-
Secrets Manager component considerations and best practices
-
According to system requirements, do not exceed the total number of supported Safes, the accounts per component, or the number of Secrets Manager components per Vault architecture. For more information, see Digital Vault server.
-
Set the refresh interval the Secrets Manager component to 25 minutes or more.
-
The cache capability must be enabled.
Setting the refresh interval to less than 25 minutes or disabling the cache capability may result in degradation and instability of the Vault performance.
Example
Scenario
The Secrets Manager component (Credential Providers) is installed on a server that serves three applications. The Secrets Manager component needs access to a total of 10 accounts. These accounts are stored in two different Safes because the other applications installed on the server are managed by different teams.
Implementation
Using a human user, create two dedicated Safes for the Credential Providers component. Configure the Safes with the following settings:
-
OLAC disabled
-
For Saved accounts, select Save the last account versions, with a value of 2
-
Set the CPM to manage the relevant platforms
-
For both Safes, configure the human owners who need access to the Safes
The policy for the accounts in the Safes has Access workflow policies disabled.
Identify the Credential Provider user name used for this server and create the accounts that you need in the dedicated Safes created for this Credential Provider.
Verify that each Safe does not have any other Secrets Manager user that is an owner of the Safe, and add the Credential Provider user as an owner of the Safe.
FAQs
When you add permissions to a Safe, the permissions apply to all the secrets in the Safe. In order to determine if you should add a user to a Safe, and which permissions the human user should have, follow the least privilege best practices below:
-
If all human users should have the same access to the accounts in the Safe, add the user to the Safe.
-
If a human user doesn't need access to all the accounts in the Safe, separate the accounts into a different Safe.
-
Follow the best practices above for new Safes.

Certificate Requirements
It is highly recommended that you use your organization's SSL certificate. Otherwise, you can use the self-signed certificate created during PTA installation.
If you use your organization's SSL certificate:
- The SSL Certificate requires a Base-64 or DER encoded X.509 SSL certificate
- The SSL Certificate requires both Server authentication and Client authentication Enhanced Key Usage values
- The SSL Certificate Chain requires a Base-64 or DER encoded X.509 SSL certificate
- The SSL Certificate Issuer Chain requires a Base-64 or DER encoded X.509 SSL certificate
- The Signature Algorithm of the SSL Certificate cannot be RSASSA-PSS
-
The hash algorithm must be SHA-256 or higher
You can upload certificates to the PTA server signed with SHA-1 signature algorithms.
While CyberArk recommends using signature algorithms that are SHA-256 and higher only, to ensure a more secured authentication channel, customers who do not have this option in their organization can use the SHA1 option.
A new parameter, enable_insecure_certificate_signatures, was added to the systemparm.properties configuration file, with a default value of False. Set the parameter to True to enable uploading certificates signed with SHA-1 signature algorithms to the PTA server.
For more information about PTA certificates, see PTA Certificate Procedures.
SSL Certificate Subject section
The SSL Certificate Subject section must include at least one of the following Distinguished Name values:
-
DC: Domain Component
-
O: Organization
The SSL Certificate should have either the local host name or the local host IP in either of the following sections:
-
Subject
-
CN: Common Name
-
-
Subject Alternative Name
-
DNS: DNS name
-
IP: IP address
-

Connect through PSM for SSH
This topic describes transparent connections to SSH target systems through PSM for SSH.
Overview
The Privileged Session Manager for SSH (PSM for SSH) enables you to connect to remote SSH systems and devices with a native user experience through any SSH client, such as plink, PuTTY, SecureCrt.
You require the Use accounts and List accounts permissions in the Safe to connect transparently to remote machines.
You can authenticate to the Vault through PSM for SSH using the following methods:
- CyberArk password
- LDAP
- RADIUS including Challenge-Response
- SSH Key
- Smart card authentication
For information about configuring authentication methods that will be available for PSM for SSH connections in your environment, refer to Authentication Methods.
|
To use SSH Key or Smart card with MFA caching, you must have SSH 7.8 or higher installed on the PSM for SSH machine. |
PSM for SSH Command
This section describes how to access target machines using the PSM for SSH commands.
PSM for SSH can be used by any ssh client using one of the following syntaxes:
<ssh client> [-t] [-i <PrivateKeyFile>] [-L <LocalPort>:127.0.0.1:<TunnelingServerPort>] <VaultUser>@<TargetUser>[#<DomainAddress>]@<TargetAddress>[#<TargetPort>[#<ForwardPort>]]@<ProxyAddress> [<Command>] |
-
Parameters are separated by ‘@’.
-
Required parameters are separated from optional parameters by ‘#’ (hash sign).
You can customize the default delimiters that are used by PSM for SSH (‘@’, ‘#’). For example, you can change the ‘@’ delimiter to enable connections with a domain or other user names that include this character. For information about configuring PSM for SSH syntax delimiters see PSM for SSH Syntax Delimiter .
The syntax described in Option 1 can be extended. This syntax starts with a general delimiter and can have additional parameters configured at the end. There are two preconfigured general delimiters: + and |.
For example:
+<ssh client> [-t] [-i <PrivateKeyFile>] [-L <LocalPort>:127.0.0.1:<TunnelingServerPort>] <VaultUser>@<TargetUser>[#<DomainAddress>]@<TargetAddress>[#<TargetPort>][#<ForwardPort>][+ticketid+<TicketID>][+ticketingsystem+<TicketingSystem>]@<ProxyAddress> [<Command>] |
or:
<ssh client> [-t] [-i <PrivateKeyFile>] [-L <LocalPort>:127.0.0.1:<TunnelingServerPort>] "|<VaultUser>@<TargetUser>[#<DomainAddress>]@<TargetAddress>[#<TargetPort>][#<ForwardPort>][|ticketid|<TicketID>][|ticketingsystem|<TicketingSystem>]@<ProxyAddress>" [<Command>] |
The additional parameters can be added in a +key+value form or |key|value form. In the above examples, ticketid is the key name of the parameter and <TicketID> is the actual value of the parameter.
Each parameter has its preconfigured name and some additional aliases. The full list of parameter names and aliases can be found in the description for Option 3.
<ssh client> [-t] [-i <PrivateKeyFile>] [-L <LocalPort>:127.0.0.1:<TunnelingServerPort>] [-R <RemoteTunnelingPsmpServerPort>:127.0.0.1:<LocalPort>] +vaultuser+<VaultUser>+targetuser+<TargetUser>[+domainaddress+<DomainAddress>]+targetaddress+<TargetAddress>[+targetport+<TargetPort>][+forwardport+<ForwardPort>][+remoteport+<RemotePort>][+ticketid+<TicketID>][+ticketingsystem+<TicketingSystem>]@<ProxyAddress> [<Command>] |
In this option, you can provide all connection parameters in a +key+value form or |key|value form. Each parameter has its own preconfigured alias. The names and aliases can be used interchangeably.
Make sure that all TunnelingServerPort parameters are pointing to consecutive ports of the port range specified in the TunnelingPorts parameter. For details, see Enable SSH tunneling in PVWA.
Remote forwarding multiple ports can be achieved in the same manner, where RemoteTunnelingPorts contains allowed ports and RemoteTunnelingServerPorts contains the range of uniquely selected ports that SSH users need to select to activate forwarding in PSM for SSH.
