Scan for accounts using Account Discovery
This topic presents the account discovery capability, which scans your domain machines to discover privileged accounts and their dependencies in your organization. Discovered accounts are displayed for analysis in the Privilege Cloud Portal or by running dedicated REST APIs. You then decide which accounts should be securely managed by Privilege Cloud and add them to the system - this process is called onboarding.
This section explains how to configure Account Discovery scans, review discovered accounts, and onboard them.
What accounts can you discover?
Account Discovery discovers the following types of accounts:
-
Windows domain and local accounts
-
Unix local accounts and SSH Keys
-
MacOS accounts from within the Administrators/root groups
These accounts are grouped into two categories:
-
Pending accounts. Pending accounts are privileged accounts in your organization, which you may want to secure by applying a privileged access policy based on password or key. Scan mechanisms provide a list of potential pending accounts, allowing you to review and analyze them, and then decide whether to onboard them to Privilege Cloud, or discard them from the list.
Learn more about pending accountsDiscovered accounts for Windows and Unix machines are displayed in the Pending Accounts list for analysis
After analyzing an account, you can decide whether to onboard it to the system or delete it from the list.
Learn more in How Accounts Discovery works .
-
Account dependencies. Account dependencies provide additional information related to the discovered accounts and indicate additional locations where an account's secrets should be changed, for example, a Windows service, or a Windows scheduled task. Account dependencies should be taken into consideration and handled when onboarding new accounts.
Learn more about account dependenciesAccount dependencies can be discovered for:
-
Pending accounts. These are reflected in the Pending Accounts list by updating the counter of the account dependencies.
-
Existing accounts, which are already defined in Privilege Cloud. When account discovery identifies new dependencies associated with an existing domain account, Privilege Cloud automatically adds them to the account. Due to risk of malicious dependencies, they are added by default in disabled mode. Admins must review and verify each newly discovered dependency, and only then approve it for for CPM secret management.
-
How Accounts Discovery works
The CPM Scanner service scans Windows and Unix machines for new and modified accounts and their dependencies. The discovered accounts are displayed in the Pending Accounts feed for review. You can then decide to onboard, disregard, or delete each discovered account.
-
Scanned machines. The account scan runs according to a defined source such as your organization's Active Directory or a CSV file.
-
Supported machines. The CPM Scanner service supports Windows and Unix machines, see Supported target machines.
-
Default component. The CPM Scanner service is installed automatically, as part of the Connector installation.
-
Required permissions. See Permissions required for running an account discovery scan.
-
Setup and configuration. To set up and configure the CPM Scanner - see Configure the CPM Scanner.
-
Perform account discovery and onboarding. See Discover accounts using the CPM Scanner.
Account types
Discovered accounts are grouped into the following categories:
|
Account type |
Description |
|---|---|
|
Pending accounts |
Accounts discovered by the CPM Scanner. Discovered accounts are displayed in Privilege Cloud Portal, in the Pending Accounts list. |
|
Dependent accounts |
Account dependencies provide additional information related to the discovered accounts and indicate additional locations where an account's secrets should be changed, for example, a Windows service or a Windows scheduled task. Account dependencies can be discovered for:
|
The Accounts Discovery process
Onboarding accounts is a continuous process, where each account goes through three steps:
Scan your environment to discover accounts that require privileged access.
- Manual vs. scheduled scans. You can run scans once or schedule recurring scans. Recurring scans update pending accounts and the account dependencies.
-
Automatic update of dependencies. When a new dependency is discovered, it is added to the pending account dependencies. If the account is already onboarded, newly detected dependencies are automatically onboarded as well.
-
Running account discovery on remote Unix machines. Some organizations block privileged access to remote Unix machines. In this case, a dedicated logon account with permission to logon remotely is required to log on to the remote machine. After this logon account has authenticated to the remote machine, the privileged user can run discoveries. In these environments, before creating discoveries, associate a logon account to the account that will be used to run discoveries on remote Unix machines. For more information about creating and associating logon accounts, see Create linked accounts.
The results of the scan are placed in a queue in the Pending Accounts list. Review the Pending Accounts list, assess the risk of each account, and select which accounts to onboard, and which are no longer needed and can be deleted.
Onboard accounts and assign them to a Safe and platform. You can also use onboarding rules to automatically assign accounts to Safes as soon as they are discovered.

Send PTA syslog Records to SIEM
PTA can integrate with any SIEM solution that supports RFC3164 or RFC5424 to send detected incidents as syslog messages.
This section describes how to configure outbound integration of PTA with your SIEM solution.
You can identify PTA records by their device vendor name, CyberArk, and their device product name, PTA.
Configure SIEM outbound connectivity for PTA to send syslog records to SIEM
Use the following procedure to configure SIEM outbound connectivity.
|
Configure SIEM outbound connectivity for PTA
-
In PVWA, click the PTA Administration tab in the Administration pane and select SIEM outbound connectivity.
The SIEM outbound connectivity page appears.
-
Click Add SIEM to set the SIEM system connectivity details.
-
Enter the SIEM system name.
-
Enter the relevant SIEM system server address in FQDN or IPv4 format.
-
Enter the Port where the syslog records will be sent from PTA to the target SIEM solution. Validate that this port is accessible on the SIEM server.
-
Select the transfer protocol.
-
If a secure protocol (TLS) is chosen, click Browse to navigate to the dedicated security Base-64 encoded X.509 SSL certificate of the SIEM server or the root CA certificate. Only a .crt, .cer, or .pem file is supported.
-
Select the certificate file, click Open, and then click OK.
-
Select the syslog header format.
-
Select the format of the syslog records.
To see the syslog records format definitions sent by PTA, see CEF-Based Format Definition and LEEF-Based Format Definition.
-
Click the Enable octet-counting toggle if you'd like the syslog message to start with its length.
-
Click Save.
-
Click Add SIEM to add another SIEM system and enter the necessary details.
-
Click Remove to delete a specific SIEM solution.
The connectivity status to the SIEM servers is verified each time the page is loaded.
Test PTA syslog records to SIEM configuration

|
If no error is shown on the screen, check the configured SIEM for the test syslog record from PTA.

JWT validation
JWT validation is a security layer that ensures that only authenticated sessions are allowed via HTML5 Gateway. When a user establishes an HTML5 connection through PVWA, the HTTP response includes JWT, which is used by HTML5 Gateway to validate the HTTP request by the client. When validation fails the connection is not established.
Requirements
- Vault 11.5 or higher
- PVWA 11.5 or higher
- HTML5 Gateway 11.6 or higher
Configuration:
- EnableJWTValidation is enabled by default.
- Value EndPointAddress with the PVWA URL. For details, see Configure the HTML5 Webapp or Run the container.
- Communication between the PSM HTML5 Gateway and the API that generates the token for JWT validation (PVWA) uses an SSL certificate to provide secured communication. Therefore, the PVWA certificate must be imported to the HTML5 Gateway. For details, see Secure the webapp and JWT validation endpoint or Map a directory for certificates and related files.

Automate with the Identity Security (idsec) Terraform provider
This topic introduces the CyberArk Identity Security Terraform Provider (idsec), which enables automation of CyberArk operations using Hashicorp Terraform.
This topic is relevant if your user access policies are managed in the Administration space (under Access control policies) or using the Access control policies API.
If your access policies are managed in SCA's Policies page, or using the SCA Policies API, see Automate with the SCA provider for Terraform.
Migrated CyberArk tenants: If, before the migration, your organization was using the SCA Terraform Provider to automate Secure Cloud Access operations, the automation will continue to work in the migrated tenant, but no more enhancements will be added. In addition, you need to make sure that all your policies have unique names.
Recommended: To take full advantage of ongoing support and future improvements for automation with Terraform, we strongly recommend redefining your automation using the unified idsec Terraform Provider, described in this topic.
Overview
Terraform is a leading Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tool that automates the deployment and management of IT infrastructure (like servers, networks, and cloud services).
The CyberArk Identity Security Terraform Provider enables IT, infrastructure, and development teams to define and automate CyberArk configurations as Infrastructure as Code (IaC). This delivers consistent security, reduces operational risk, and accelerates deployment speed across all cloud and on-premises environments.
This solution ensures that identity and access controls scale securely alongside your critical infrastructure, maintaining full auditability and least-privilege control at every step.
For more information, see CyberArk Identity Security Terraform Provider.
Supported SCA operations
You can use the idsec Terraform provider to include the following SCA operations in your Hashicorp Terraform automation:

Discover updates to a workspace that is already onboarded to CyberArk

The Privileged Session Management UI parameters of the Configuration Options determine how PSM-related items are displayed in the PVWA, as well as the user experience during PSM sessions.
User experience
The following general Privileged Session Management UI parameters configure the user experience for PSM sessions and define which method used to establish the connection:
|
Parameter |
Description |
|---|---|
|
UseRemoteApp |
This parameter determines whether or not PSM sessions are displayed in a standard client window, facilitating an intuitive user experience. This is only relevant when PSM connections are established using an RDP file. You can disable RemoteApp user experience for each connection component by setting the parameter DisableRemoteApp for the relevant connection component. |
You can configure PSM to provide secure remote access to a target machine through an HTML5 gateway. With HTML5 connections, the session to the remote machine is displayed in a browser regardless of the settings in the table above.

View high risk sessions
PSM can integrate with CyberArk Privileged Threat Analytics (PTA) in order to analyze the details of PSM privileged sessions and user activities in each session. The PTA receives details of each session and analyzes them, and then assigns a risk score. This score is sent to the Vault when it is created and when it is updated in real time as the session proceeds. The risk score is displayed in the PVWA MONITORING page, in the PSM recordings details for active sessions and for privileged sessions that have already finished. For more information about PTA functionality and risk scores, refer to the PTA Implementation Guide.
The following workflow describes how to configure PSM to integrate with PTA and display risk scores for privileged sessions.
| 1. | Configure PSM connections so that users can access remote machines through the PSM. |
| 2. | Make sure that PSM detailed audit capabilities are enabled. For more information, refer to Configure audits. |
| 3. | Install PTA and configure it to integrate with PSM. For more information, refer to the PTA Implementation Guide. |
| 4. | In the PVWA, configure PSM integration with PTA: |
| a. | Click ADMINISTRATION, then in the System Configuration page, click Options; the Web Access Options page appears. |
| b. | Display the Privileged Session Management UI parameters and configure the following property: |
| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| PSMandPTAIntegration | The parameter determines whether or not security incident data received from PTA will be displayed. This includes the risk score column in the Sessions List and the incident details in the Recording Details page. |
| 5. | Define the Security Incident details that will be displayed in the Recording Details page and the Active Sessions page. |
| a. | Under the Privileged Session Management UI parameters, expand the Recording Details parameters, and then Recordings Security Incidents Properties. |
| b. | Select the Displayed Properties parameters, and set the following properties: |
| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| IncidentName |
The name of the security incident.
Default value: Name |
| IncidentID |
The unique ID of the security incident.
Default value: ID |
| IncidentLink |
A link to the PTA page that displays more information about the security incident.
Default value: URL |
| RiskScore |
The risk score that was allocated to the security incident.
Default value: Risk Score |
| IncidentStartDate |
The date and time when the security incident began.
Default value: Incident Start Date |
| Activity |
The activity that caused a security incident.
Default value: Highest Risk Activity |
| ActivityOffset |
The length of time after the privileged session started that the risk activity was performed.
Default value: Activity Offset from Start of Session |
| 6. | Click Apply to save these configurations and apply them. |

Standard Ports used for Accounts Discovery
The CyberArk CPM Scanner uses the following ports to discover accounts and SSH keys on remote machines:
|
Port |
Use case |
|---|---|
|
22 |
To connect to target machines using SSH. This port can be configured by the SSHPort parameter in the CACPMScanner.exe.config file. |
|
88 |
Used for KDC services (only relevant to domain controllers). This port must be accessible both through network-based and host-based firewalls. |
|
135, 137, 138, 139 |
To connect to target machines using NetBIOS ports. These ports must be accessible on host-based firewalls. |
|
389 |
To connect to target machines using the LDAP service (only relevant to domain controllers). This port must be accessible both through network-based and host-based firewalls. |
|
636 |
To connect to target machines using the LDAPS service (only relevant to domain controllers). This port must be accessible both through network-based and host-based firewalls. |
|
445 |
To connect to target machines using SMB/TCP. This port must be accessible on host-based firewalls. |
|
4431 |
To discover SSH keys on Windows machines without Cygwin. This port is not configurable. |
|
49154 |
This port is used to view and administrate Scheduled Tasks on the remote machine. |
|
49155, 49156 |
This port is used to get the list of services from the remote machine. |
|

Enable WMI Ports on Windows Client Machines
To enable the Windows (WMI) Protocol in your environment:
| 1. | Make sure the Windows Management Instrumentation service startup type is set to Automatic. |
| 2. | For your operating system, do the following: |
| ■ | Windows 7 - In the firewall settings for your local or Group policy, under Inbound Rules, make sure Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI-In) is enabled and allowed for the Domain profile. |
| ■ | Windows Vista - In the firewall settings for your local or Group policy, click the Exceptions tab and enable the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) exception. |
| ■ | Windows XP - Run the following commands from the commands prompt: |
| ■ | netsh firewall set service RemoteAdmin enable. |
| ■ | netsh firewall add portopening protocol=tcp port=135 name=DCOM_TCP135. |
| ■ | netsh firewall set portopening tcp 445 smb enable. |

On-demand access enhancements
Allowed identities
Cloud management is a sensitive resource because it allows access to all of your cloud services. As such, user access should be limited to those identities that are authorized administrators of the workspaces they want to access. With the new allowed identities feature, organizations can allow only certain identities to request access or elevated permissions to cloud management consoles.
Context-aware automatic approval
Additionally, as part of the on-demand access workflow organizations can now define the default approval method, either automatic or manual. Along with the default approval method, exceptions can be defined for identities that meet certain conditions.
For example, an organization can define the default approval method as manual, meaning all on-demand access requests must be handled by an administrator. However, if an identity submits a request to access a workspace tagged as "staging", this poses little to no risk so the request can be approved automatically.
Using this new capability, organizations can enforce security guidelines while reducing the workload for approvers, enabling them to handle only higher-risk access requests.

SCA now provides a solution for both needs. Organizations can benefit from regular policy-based access for daily users, and on-demand access for unplanned or infrequent situations that require immediate attention for a critical issue. On-demand access enables users to request access to specific workspaces at specific times. With this new capability, organizations can further reduce exposure due to excessive privileges and grant elevated permissions only when actually required.
On-demand access comes with an out-of-the-box integration with Slack, and can be customized for other ChatOps channels or ticketing systems.
Support for Azure AD
Azure AD includes highly privileged roles such as Global Administrator. To keep cloud environments secure, organizations need a way to assign these roles on a Just-In-Time basis for sessions that are limited in length.
SCA introduces Just-In-Time access and privilege elevation for Microsoft Azure AD roles. This capability helps organizations improve their security posture and reduce risk by granting least-privilege, on-demand access to Azure AD roles for daily operations using SCA policies. Using SCA, cloud security administrators can grant Just-In-Time access to Azure AD roles at the tenant level. Users can access their Azure cloud environment from either the Azure management portal or the Azure CLI.
With this new enhancement, SCA now fully supports Microsoft Azure, with both Azure AD and Azure RBAC functionality.

Overview
After you have reviewed the list of discovered accounts, you can decide on your next step, whether you want to:
-
Define rules to automate onboarding. See View and manage remediation rules.
-
Manually onboard certain accounts and remove others. See Onboard accounts manually.
Review and analyze discovered accounts
-
In Identity Protection, click Discovery & Remediations > Discovered Identities > Accounts.
The Account List displays all discovered accounts. An icon indicates the account type.
-

Search option
Description
Filter
Click Filter and define parameters to filter the account list.
The list is updated according to your selected filters. The filters are displayed at the top of the account list together with the total number of matching accounts.
Click Clear All to remove your selected filters.
Search
In the text entry field, start typing the name or string that appears for the account of interest. The search is case-insensitive.
The account list is filtered to display matching accounts.

- Click an account in the grid to open the split view and see account details on the right side.
-

You can temporarily exclude specific discovered accounts from onboarding. For example, you might want to ignore accounts that are not ready for management, such as personal accounts, low-privilege accounts, or accounts you plan to onboard later.
When you ignore an account, the system excludes it from future discovery results until you remove it from the ignore list.

Select a discovered account.

Click Move account.

-

Select an account that you no longer want to ignore.
-
In the Overview tab, click the More actions button (...) and select Restore.

Configure automatic reconnection
This topic describes how to configure automatic reconnection in PSM sessions.
The PSM supports automatic reconnection of disconnected sessions. In the event of a temporary network disruption, sessions seamlessly reconnect, minimizing workflow interruptions and improving reliability for end users.
Automatic reconnection is supported for Client <> PSM server interface.
Automatic reconnection is not supported for sessions launched through HTML5 Gateway.
Enable session reconnection
To enable session reconnection, you must configure the Session Time Limit policy in the GPO.
-
In the PSM installation directory, in the basic_psm.ini configuration file, set EnableSessionReconnection=Yes.
-
Set the following group policies:
-
EnableAutoReconnect = Enabled
-
RemoteAppLogoffTimeLimit = 1 minute (6000)
-
MaxDisconnectionTime = 1 minute (6000)
In the Group Policy editor, go to Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Session Time Limits and double-click on Set time limit for disconnected sessions and Set time limit for logoff of RemoteApp sessions. Set the time limits to one minute.
The session recordings will be available on the Recordings page after the time configured in the Session Time Limit policy.
-
-
Make sure that the RDP client allows session reconnection.
-
Restart the PSM machine.
If you're using a load balancer to manage sessions on multiple instances, enable sticky sessions (also known as session affinity) on the load balancer to ensure that user requests are consistently routed to the same instance throughout a session.
Limitations
-
Session reconnection is supported for RDP client connections. Other connections, such as .nix targets, are not supported.
-
In HTML5 Gateway sessions, the end user does not receive an indication during the reconnection window.
-
Session reconnection is disabled during live monitored sessions.
-
Session reconnection is not applied for MAC clients.
If you use the Suspend capability, do not enable the session reconnection feature. To use the session reconnection feature, use the Terminate option.

Automatic password management is supported on MySQL Server accounts on IPv4 and IPv6.
The MySQL Server plugin is available for both 32-bit and 64-bit architecture.
Starting from MySQL Server platform version 21.0, Database Credentials Management Framework version 14.5 must be used.

The CPM supports remote password management on a MySQL Server on the following platforms:

MySQL Server version 8.4, 9.5 (64-bit)
-
MySQL Server version 8 (32-bit)
For customers with existing platforms that are linked to the MySQLServer Server 32-bit plugin for MySQLServer version 8 with a 32-bit driver, you can upgrade to the MySQLServer Server 64-bit plugin for MySQLServer version 8.4 and later with a 64-bit driver.

-

Password Management Features
The CPM can change and verify MySQL Server passwords on remote machines, and can reconcile these passwords with local accounts. If a password is invalid, the CPM can generate a new password and replace the invalid password on the remote machine and its corresponding password in the Password Vault. The parameters that define these tasks are in the platform. A reconciliation account password can be specified either at platform level or at account level.

Manage virtual machine access
This section describes how to onboard and manage virtual machine targets for access using vaulted credentials.
-
If you have PSM installed in parallel to SIA, none of the PSM configuration affects VM vaulted access using SIA.

SIA policies (those that are relevant for zero standing privileges cases) do not apply when using SIA for vaulted access.
-
In this section, reference to accessing virtual machines also includes access to physical machines.
Virtual machine access workflow
The following is an outline of the workflow to enable access to virtual machines using SIA and vaulted credentials. It is assumed the administrator has already set the Master policy and created Safes.
-
Add virtual machine accounts. For more information, see Manage your accounts.
The following are supported:
-
Windows local accounts.
-
Windows domain accounts.
-
Linux SSH accounts.
-
Linux domain accounts.
-
Linux accounts with SSH keys. Supported formats are OpenSSH SSH key and Putty Private Key (PPK).
To define these accounts, you must populate the account properties. For more information, see Account properties.
-
-
Add connectors. For more information, see Add connectors.
-
Configure settings as appropriate. For more information, see Manage settings.
-
Add certificates. For more information, see Manage certificates .
-
Only for RDP connections with a vaulted credential and elevated permission:
-
Configure a SIA policy for the user and specify there the local groups you want the target user to be part of.
-
Configure a strong account that will be a strong account for elevating the target user to the specified local groups.
-
-
Only for RDP connections with domain accounts, the authentication method for RDP connections is determined by the Kerberos authentication setting. For more information, see Authentication settings.
-
Connect to the target. For more information, see Connect to a Windows target and Connect to a Linux target.
After you have onboarded a virtual machine, you manage it as you manage other targets in Privilege Cloud.
Automatic logon sequence for SSH vaulted connections
This functionality is supported for Privilege Cloud, but not for PAM - Self-Hosted.
To support automatic logon sequences in SIA connections that use SSH vaulted accounts, you must define the AutoLogonSequence parameter in the relevant PSM-SSH or PSMP-SSH connection components in Privilege Cloud. For more information, see Logon sequence hierarchy.
The AutoLogonSequence parameter specifies a multi-line sequence using regular expression prompts and responses that automate interaction with the target system during login.
To use this capability, set the SSH logon sequence with logon account parameter in SIA to Only when the sequence is not defined in Privilege Cloud. For more information, see Automatic SSH logon sequence.
If the AutoLogonSequence parameter is not defined in Privilege Cloud, no logon sequence will be applied, and the automatic sign-on process will not be executed.
Logon sequence with logon account for SSH vaulted connections
This functionality is supported for Privilege Cloud, but not for PAM - Self-Hosted.
You can use a logon account to initiate sessions on machines that do not allow direct privileged access. This account is used to log on to the remote machine and then elevates its privileges to a privileged user role using credentials stored in the Vault.
You can configure how SIA performs the logon and privilege elevation processes by using the Automatic SSH logon sequence with logon account setting as follows:
-
To apply a single logon sequence for all logon accounts that are configured in SIA, do the following:
-
Set the Automatic SSH logon sequence with logon account setting to Always
-
Define a shell logon sequence
-
-
To apply specific logon sequences for various targets, set the Automatic SSH logon sequence with logon account setting to Only when the sequence is not defined in Privilege Cloud.
For more information, see Automatic SSH logon sequence and Logon sequence hierarchy.
For SSH connections, the logon account can use either password or SSH key authentication. If the logon account uses SSH key authentication, the associated privileged account must use password authentication.
Logon sequence hierarchy
SIA supports a hierarchical, multi-line logon sequence for SSH access using vaulted accounts. Before opening a session, SIA determines the appropriate logon sequence hierarchy for the end user.
SIA evaluates the settings defined in the PSM-SSH and PSMP-SSH connection components, as configured in Privilege Cloud, to determine the logon sequence. The following table shows how SIA determines the hierarchy.
|
Hierarchy |
PSM-SSH |
PSMP-SSH |
Connection component used |

|
First |
Defined |
Not defined |
PSM-SSH |
|

Not defined |
Defined |
PSMP-SSH |
|
Third |
Defined |
Defined |
PSMP-SSH |
|
Fourth Not supported for Automatic logon sequence for SSH vaulted connections |
Not defined |
Not defined |
Automatic SSH logon sequence with logon account (Default setting) |
If platform-level Override target settings are defined when the multi-line logon sequence capability is implemented:
-
SIA uses these values to determine the logon sequence hierarchy.
-
SIA ignores the Enabled property of the PSM-SSH and PSMP-SSH connection components on platform-level definitions.
-
Any subsequent changes made to the PSM-SSH or PSMP-SSH connection component values in Privilege Cloud configuration options do not affect the logon sequence. To modify the effective logon sequence, you must update the Override target settings.
This capability may cause a security risk if it is not configured correctly.
To reduce the risk:
-
Use this capability with caution, and make sure the privileged account password is never exposed to the end user.
-
Always specify the full path for binaries executed during the logon sequence (for example, /usr/bin/su).

Discover accounts using the CPM Scanner
This topic presents the work flow to discover Windows and Unix domain machine accounts using the CPM Scanner.
Before you begin
-
Learn about Supported target machines.
-
Learn about Permissions required for running an account discovery scan.
-
Configure the scanner, set Unix/Linux configuration, and start & stop the scanner - see Configure the CPM Scanner.
Step 1: Run a discovery scan
To run a scan, you must have the required permissions. See Permissions required for running an account discovery scan.
Scan Windows machines
- In the Privilege Cloud Portal, click Accounts > Pending & Discovery, and then click Discovery Management.
- On the Discovery Management page, click New Windows Discovery.
-
On the New Windows Accounts Discovery page, enter the following information:
- Domain. Specify the domain you want to scan, in FQDN format. Up to 170 characters.
-
Select the account to run the scan (typically, this is a domain administrator account). Select one of the following options:
Select from Vault Use an account that is already defined in the Vault
-
Click Click to select an account from the Vault.
- Select the account from the list, and then click Select account.
Ensure that the CPM selected for the scan has access to the Safe to which the account belongs.
Specify Account Specify an account manually
Enter the user and password.
The user must have read permissions in the OU and all sub-OUs to scan.
-
-
In OU to Scan, enter the distinguished name of the OU you want to scan (the Browse button is not available for Privilege Cloud). You can enter only one OU.
For example: dc=example,dc=com
The Privilege Cloud Portal connects to the Active Directory using the user credentials you specified.
If Connect to the Active Directory is selected, the Privilege Cloud Portal connects to the Active Directory using a secure connection.
- Set the scan to be either one time or recurring.
-
Click Done.
The scan is activated.
-
The initial state of the scan is Pending. Click the Refresh button to update the state.
One time scans are performed as soon as the scanner finishes current discoveries.
Recurrent discoveries are added to the list of pending discoveries and will be performed on the date and time.
The length of time for a scan depends on the number of resources you defined.
Scan Unix machines
-
Before creating a discovery process for Unix accounts and SSH keys, create the CSV file that contains a list of all the Unix/Linux machine addresses that will be scanned. These addresses can be listed as IP addresses, machine host names or machine FQDN (full DNS names).
Example of a csv file:
192.0.2.0
192.0.2.1
192.0.2.2
192.0.2.3
For a full list of supported Unix/Linux machines, see Accounts Feed supported target machines
- In the Privilege Cloud Portal, click Accounts > Pending & Discovery, and then click Discovery Management.
- On the Discovery Management page, click New Unix Discovery.
- On the New Unix Accounts Discovery page, enter the following information:
In Which file contains the list of machines, click Browse, then select the CSV file that lists the Unix accounts.
In Which user will scan the machines, enter the user name of the user running the scan.
In What is the user’s default password, enter the user's password.
In Which CPM scanner to use, select the CPM that will scan for Unix accounts. The CPM will scan only machines that it can physically access.
To scan for SSH keys and their trusts, select Scan SSH Keys.
In What recurring pattern to set for this Discovery, select whether you want this scan to be recurring or one time, and set the date and time.
Click Done.
One time scans are performed as soon as the scanner finishes current discoveries.
Recurrent discoveries are added to the list of pending discoveries and will be performed on the date and time.
The length of time for a scan depends on the number of resources you defined.
|
Step 2: Analyze pending accounts
After you run a scan, analyze the pending accounts and SSH keys list for onboarding.
To analyze pending accounts:
-
In the Privilege Cloud Portal, click Accounts > Pending & Discovery, and then click Pending Accounts.
The grid displays pending accounts discovered by scans and external scanners using the AddPendingAccounts Web Service.
- Use the filters in the left pane to filter the accounts in the grid, and use the column headers to sort the accounts for an easier review process.
- Click the account in the grid to display the Account Preview pane, which includes additional information to that displayed in the grid.
- After you decide which account you want to onboard, proceed to Step 3: Onboard accounts.
Step 3: Onboard accounts
You can onboard accounts and SSH keys that are displayed in the Pending Accounts page so that you can manage them automatically.
If an account contains dependencies, the dependencies are automatically onboarded with the account. A newly discovered dependency could potentially be non-legitimate or malicious. Therefore it is recommended to review and approve each newly discovered dependency to prevent such dependencies from being onboarded automatically by the system. When a discovery finds new dependencies associated with a domain account that was previously onboarded or already exists in the system, by default, the dependencies will automatically be onboarded and the account will be disabled for automatic CPM management.
When you are onboarding multiple accounts that share the same SSH key, the private SSH key will only be associated with one account. After onboarding, associate these accounts with the same group so that they can all use the same SSH key.
To onboard accounts:
- In Privilege Cloud Portal, click Accounts > Pending & Discovery.
-
On the Pending Accounts page, select the accounts, and then click Onboard Accounts.
If you select multiple accounts, make sure that they are all associated with the same platform.
-
In Store in Safe, select a Safe or create a new one. To create a Safe, see Add a new Safe.
For a Safe to display in the list you must:
- Be a member of the Safe
- Have the Add accounts permission
Internal Safes are not displayed.
-
From the Assign Platform drop-down list, select the platform.
-
In the Password section, select one of the following:
Automatically reconcile password
The passwords are reconciled automatically after they have been onboarded.
This option is only enabled for platforms that are configured for account reconciliation.
Set a default password
Specify the password that will be set in the selected accounts, and then confirm it.
This sets the passwords for the accounts in Privilege Cloud, it does not reset actual passwords on target systems. For more information about synchronizing passwords, see Manage accounts.
- Click Onboard, and when the process completes, click Done.

Configure a list of prioritized Vaults in Distributed Vaults environment for CyberArk clients
This topic describes how to configure a list of prioritized Vaults in a Distributed Vaults environment for CyberArk clients.
Overview
To provide better network connection and lower latency, Distributed Vaults architecture enables several clients to communicate directly for read-only operations with either a Primary Vault or Satellite Vault, based on the closest geographic location.
You can configure the priority list via an IP-based or DNS-SRV records to determine the communication with your Satellite Vaults.
|
The DNS-SRV record must not include a Primary Vault. |
IP-based priority list
The IP-based priority list enables client redundancy when there is a failure to connect to a specific Vault.
The priority list contains a list of Vaults that the client tries to connect to according to the order specified in the list.
When a connection cannot be established to the first Vault IP address, an attempt is initiated to connect to the next IP address on the priority list. This process continues until either a successful connection is established, or attempts to connect to all IPs on the priority list have failed.
If the client cannot connect to any Vault, the client will be isolated from the PAM - Self-Hosted environment.
In a Cluster environment, the Virtual IP (VIP) must be configured in the priority list. The first IP address on the list must always be the Vault IP that is the closest one that serves the client. The remaining Vaults in the list must be based on the same proximity.
This configuration is supported for all components and services.
|
You can provide availability of the clients connected to the Primary Vault by specifying at least the Primary Vault and the Primary Candidate Vault in the client configuration. |
DNS-SRV record
In a DNS-SRV configuration, the Vault that is accessed is determined by the DNS, according to the Vault's priority and weight. For example, the first Vault in the list will have the highest priority (the lowest number), and heaviest weight (the highest number).
If the first Vault is unavailable, the client tries to connect to the next Vault until a successful connection is established.
In a Cluster environment, the Virtual IP (VIP) must be configured in the priority list.
You can create multiple DNS-SRV records with different priority settings for the Vaults. You can also have a dedicated DNS-SRV record that includes only the Primary Vault and the Primary Candidate Vault for components that connect to the Primary Vault.
We recommend that the Vault capacity for client connections is configured no higher than 75% of the Vault capacity. This allows the Vault to handle a load of additional clients that may be assigned to the Vault during a connection failure scenario.
This configuration is only supported for Secrets Manager components.
|
The DNS SRV records must be configured to reflect the required failover order, not for load balancing. Assign each Vault entry a different priority. You can't assign the same priority to more than one Vault. |
Vault Failure
Primary Vault failure
If there is a temporary failure of the Primary Vault, and a priority list has not been configured, only read-only operations will be allowed on the Satellite Vaults.
After the Primary Vault returns to a normal operating state, the Satellite Vaults will also return to a normal operating state with read-write operations.
Users that are logged on to PVWA during a failure can continue working in the same session, but will be in read-only mode. To regain full read-write operations, users must log in to PVWA again.
If the priority list is configured during a failure of the Primary Vault, and the next vault in the list is promoted to take over as the Primary Vault, the promotion process will be completed within 3-5 minutes.
Satellite Vault failure
A Satellite Vault failure occurs as a result of one of the following scenarios:
-
A Satellite Vault is disconnected from the topology
-
A Satellite Vault fails
When a Satellite Vault fails, the clients try to connect to the next Vault specified in the client configuration file.
If a priority list is not configured, and the Satellite Vault was disconnected from the topology, the Satellite Vault can still provide read-only operations to clients. After the connection to the Primary Vault is restored, read-write operations are restored to the clients.
If a priority list is configured, and the Satellite Vault was disconnected from the topology, the Satellite Vault that is promoted will allow read-write operations to the Vault. Before reconnecting the Satellite Vault to the topology, the promoted Satellite Vault must be switched back to a regular Satellite Vault, and then manually connected back to the topology as a Satellite Vault.
There cannot be two Primary Vaults in the same environment.
|
When a failure occurs on the Primary Vault, write operations will not be available until a new Primary Vault becomes available, either after satellite promotion or after the original Primary Vault is up and running. As a result, client environments cannot be created during a Primary Vault failure. |
Configure the list of prioritized Vaults
This section describes the configuration options for the list of prioritized Vaults.
Common use cases and configurations
-
Priority list between a Primary Vault and Satellite Vaults - Use Configure an IP-based priority list
-
Priority list between Satellite Vaults - Use one of the following configurations, based on supported components and services
-
Priority list between a Primary Vault and Satellite Vaults for an Active Primary Vault only - Active Primary Vault only priority list
-
|
You cannot be connected to two different Vault types at the same time. You can only be connected to either a Primary Vault or a Satellite Vault. |
Configure an IP-based priority list
-
In the client installation folder, open the Vault.ini file.
-
If the client will connect to a Satellite Vault, add the DISTRIBUTEDVAULTS parameter, and set it to static.
DISTRIBUTEDVAULTS=static
-
Do one of the following, depending on which Vault type you are configuring the connection for:
-
For a Primary Vault in the Address parameter, specify a comma-separated IP address for the Primary Vaults and the Primary Candidate Vault.
This applies to components that connect only to the Primary Vault.
-
For the Satellite Vault, in the Address parameter, specify a comma-separated IP address for the Vaults, based on their priority, from highest to lowest.
-
-
Save the Vault.ini file, and close it.
|
Do not configure clients that directed to a Satellite Vault directly to a Primary Vault. |
Configure a DNS-SRV-based priority list
The following components and clients are supported:
-
Credential Provider
-
Export Vault Data (EVD) Utility
-
Replicate
-
PVWA
To configure DNS:
-
In a Microsoft DNS server, configure a DNS SRV:
-
Open the DNS Manager, and navigate to the folder in which you want to create the SRV record.
-
Right-click the folder, and select Other New Records
-
In the Resource Record Type list, select Service Location (SRV).
-
In the New Resource Record window, enter the details of the service, including the Service (area) and Priority.
DNS SRV records must be configured in the required failover order, not for load balancing. Assign each Vault entry a different priority (you can't assign the same priority to more than one Vault).
-
-
Define a record for each Vault and service that you want to appear in the list in the DNS server.
The following example shows three records that list the details of three Vaults. These Vaults comprise the service list for the US service.
The service name that you specify in the Client's vault.ini is comprised of the record's hierarchy. In the following example, the DNS SRV name would be US._vault.AA.provider.com.
-
Test the validity of your configuration with nslookup:
-
On a Windows machine that is configured to use your DNS server, open a Command line window, and run nslookup.
-
Specify the following information:
-
server server_address - for example, server 10.10.1.1
-
set type=SRV
-
DNS SRV name - for example, US._vault.AA.provider.com
A list of Vaults, their priorities, and additional data is returned.
-
-
-
In the client installation folder, open the Vault.ini file.
-
If the client connects to a Satellite Vault, add the DISTRIBUTEDVAULTS parameter, and set it to yes.
DISTRIBUTEDVAULTS=yes
-
In the Address parameter, enter an address that returns a DNS SRV record.
-
Save and close the Vault.ini file.
Active Primary Vault only priority list
-
In the client installation folder, open the Vault.ini file.
-
Delete the DISTRIBUTEDVAULTS parameter.
-
Modify the Address parameter: specify a comma-separated IP address for the Primary Vault and the Primary Candidate Vaults.
-
Save and close the Vault.ini file.
|
Clients can only connect to the active Primary Vault. |

Support for TLS protocol version 1.3
Version 14.6 introduces support for TLS protocol version 1.3, improving performance with a faster handshake and zero round-trip time for connection resumption. Based on OpenSSL 3.1, which assures FIPS 140-3 compliance, TLS v1.3 enhances security by removing weak cipher suites and using stronger cryptographic algorithms. PAM SH remains compatible with TLS v1.2 as well.
For information about which capabilities are now supporting TLS v1.3, see TLS communication protocol limitations.
Connector Management support for installations and upgrades of PSM and CPM LTS versions
We are excited to introduce PSM and CPM integration with the Connector Management service—a new capability that simplifies and streamlines the installation and upgrade of PSM and CPM servers.
This integration provides a centralized, intuitive experience for managing PSM and CPM deployments, enabling you to perform installations and upgrades with greater efficiency, visibility, and control. By consolidating operations within the Connector Management service, this enhancement reduces complexity and helps ensure consistency across environments.
This feature is available to PAM Self-Hosted customers with a subscription license and platform tenant.
This update is part of our continued commitment to delivering a modern, user-friendly experience while increasing operational efficiency.
Vault
Disaster Recovery (DR) replication enhancements
We’re excited to introduce a powerful set of enhancements that elevate the resilience, visibility, and operational efficiency of your DR replication environment
-
Reinforced resilience - We’ve resolved key issues affecting DR replication to deliver a more stable and dependable experience, ensuring your critical data is always protected and recoverable when it matters most..
-
Smarter monitoring with System Health - Gain real-time visibility into DR file and data replication directly from the PVWA System Health dashboard. Instantly spot issues before they escalate. Plus, with full REST API support, you can seamlessly integrate DR health insights into your existing monitoring tools and automation pipelines.
-
Expanded DR logging for greater visibility - DR activity logs have been enriched to offer deeper operational insights, making it easier to understand replication behavior and accelerate troubleshooting when it counts.
-
Smarter MySQL Configuration - Optimized MySQL settings now deliver faster, more stable replication with reduced network overhead and no data gaps, boosting overall DR performance and reliability.
Together, these enhancements reinforce a more robust and transparent DR experience, empowering your teams to stay ahead of disruptions and maintain a strong recovery posture.
Export Vault Data (EVD) – lightning fast LogList reports
We’ve turbocharged the EVD LogList report engine to deliver faster insights and greater control, helping you work smarter and respond quicker. Accelerated Report Generation Audit data is now intelligently distributed across long-term and short-term tables, enabling rapid access to recent activity. The result? Significantly faster LogList report generation and a smoother experience for administrators.

Take charge of your audit performance with two new configuration options:

EnableLogsumOptimizations – Activates the optimized search logic for LogList reports.
-

For setup guidance, see DBParm.ini.
These enhancements are part of our ongoing commitment to improving audit data access, system efficiency, and administrator productivity.
MySQL upgrade to LTS Version 8.4.3
In this release, we’ve upgraded the underlying MySQL database to the Long-Term Support (LTS) version 8.4.3, delivering enhanced performance, stability, and future compatibility.
This version is aligned with the latest Long-Term Support release for improved maintainability, support, and security, as well as offering enhanced stability and performance, even under sustained system activity.
This upgrade includes changes required to ensure full compatibility with MySQL 8.4.3.
To minimize downtime and avoid replication issues, CyberArk strongly recommends that you verify the health of your Disaster Recovery (DR) environment before initiating the upgrade process.
SNMP upgrade to version 3 - Secure, standards-based monitoring
We’ve upgraded to SNMP version 3, delivering a more secure and flexible foundation for network monitoring and management, built for today’s compliance-driven environments.
This version aligns with modern best practices for network security and compliance and offers:
-
User-Based authentication - Ensuring only authorized users can access SNMP data.
-
Encrypted Communication - Protecting sensitive monitoring information in transit.
-
Granular Access Control - Enabling fine-tuned permissions for SNMP operations.
SNMP v3 addresses the limitations of earlier versions by introducing robust mechanisms for authentication, privacy, and access control, making it the recommended choice for environments with elevated security and regulatory requirements.

Central Policy Manager
Advanced password security and customization
We’re pleased to announce enhancements to our password policy rules designed to enhance security, force stronger and more flexible password policies, and better meet your organization's security policies and compliance requirements. The new rules are applicable per platform, providing flexibility and ensuring compliance to the different vendors' requirements, and are enforced both by CPM and manual password change. Privileged Session Manager
Automatic session reconnection for RDP sessions after network disruption
Automatic reconnection is now supported for PSM-RDP sessions, including those launched via HTML5 Gateway. In the event of a temporary network disruption, sessions will seamlessly reconnect, minimizing workflow interruptions and improving reliability for end users. This enhancement ensures a smoother remote access experience, especially in environments with intermittent connectivity, and reduces the need to restart sessions or reauthenticate.
For details, see Configure automatic reconnection.
Introducing PSM-OpenSSH for FIPS compliancy and smart card authentication for secure SSH access
Introducing PSM-OpenSSH alongside PSM-SSH (based on PuTTY) within PSM. This enhancement provides a FIPS-compliant SSH client that enables smart card authentication at the target level, delivering a higher standard of security, particularly for customers with strict compliance requirements.
Personalized keyboard layout selection for each HTML5GW session
PAM Self-Hosted now empowers users to select their preferred keyboard layout at the start of each PSM-HTML5 Gateway session. This new capability improves usability and accessibility in multi-language environments, especially where shared targets require different keyboard configurations. By enabling users to choose the appropriate layout per session, this feature reduces input errors and enhances the overall user experience, ensuring smoother, more accurate remote access for global teams.
Enforce PKI-based authentication for PSM for Windows
Administrators can now enforce PKI (smart card) authentication for users connecting through PSM for Windows, ensuring that only certificate-based logins are permitted. This added layer of security helps meet strict compliance requirements and eliminates fallback to username/password methods, strengthening identity assurance and protecting access to sensitive targets.
AutoIT-based connection components support for 64-bit
PSM now supports 64-bit AutoIt-based connectors. This enhancement marks a significant step forward in performance and compatibility.
Custom connectors can now be compiled and executed in 64-bit, aligning with modern system architectures and improving performance.
Privileged Session Manager for SSH
PSM for SSH deployment on Ubuntu servers
PSM for SSH can now be deployed on Ubuntu v. 22.04 servers, expanding flexibility for organizations standardizing on Ubuntu as part of their infrastructure. This enhancement enables broader adoption of secure privileged session monitoring in diverse environments, without requiring changes to operating system preferences, streamlining deployment and aligning with modern IT strategies.
Extended SSH agent forwarding support for PSM for SSH
Building on the existing support for agent forwarding and smart card authentication, PSM for SSH now enables the forwarded SSH agent to be used for initiating outbound connections from the target machine to additional systems. This enhancement enables secure, seamless authentication for chained SSH sessions, improving administrator productivity while maintaining strong identity assurance across multiple hops.
Command and access control multiline paste with bracketed paste mode functionality
PSM for SSH now supports bracketed paste mode, a terminal feature that distinguishes between pasted and typed input. This enhancement significantly improves the handling of multi-line command pastes, preserving formatting, reducing errors, and ensuring commands execute as intended, especially in complex access and command control scenarios. It resolves common issues like unexpected end-of-line characters, offering a smoother experience for administrators working with terminal-based workflows.

Security enhancements
Vault security improvements
Several third-party components were upgraded to enhance security and keep up with industry standards. The most significant change is introducing OpenSSL 3.1 which not only improves security but also is an important part of the TLS protocol upgrade to version 1.3 and assures compliance with FIPS 140-3. Due to this change, there are some additional steps required to make standalone components, like EVD, FIPS compliant.
Instructions can be found in FIPS compliance changes for standalone executables in version 14.6.
PTA security improvements
Internal components, core dependencies, and third-party libraries were upgraded to enhance security and implement technological improvements in the PTA components.
The PTA core dependency Apache ActiveMQ was upgraded to version 6.1.6.
Other components
Rest APIs framework for plugins
The framework simplifies the creation of plugins for REST API services and ensures secure management of credentials. In addition, it also facilitates better integration and automation through a standardized XML schema.
The solution is an easy-to-use framework for creating plugins that works with REST APIs. Customers can create an XML based on a provided schema, specifying the required operations "verify," "change," and "reconcile." The XML also includes attributes for the necessary REST APIs and response processing.
The new REST API Application CPM Plugin Framework can be found in the CyberArk Marketplace.
ODBC new framework for Oracle
We are excited to introduce our enhanced Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) framework, designed to deliver improved security, optimized performance, and seamless compatibility with modern Oracle platforms.
Supported Oracle Instant Client versions are:
-
21.8 - Version 14.5.0 and above
-
19.8 - Version 14.5.0 and above
Oracle Unified Directory (OUD)
Support for managing privileged accounts in Oracle Unified Directory (OUD) is now available from the Marketplace.
Organizations can now automate the secure management of privileged credentials, improving security, compliance, and efficiency.
Web Application CPM Plugin Framework
To enable better management of complex web pages the Web Application CPM Plugin Framework has been enhanced to handle web pages containing multiple layers of nested iFrames (inline frames) ensuring a seamless user experience.
iFrames are commonly used to embed external and third-party content within a web page, such as loading external web pages, embedding videos and more.
With this update, the Web Application CPM plugins can better manage complex web pages that rely on multiple layers of iFrames, ensuring a seamless user experience.
The Web Application CPM Plugin Framework now supports both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of Chrome. The 64-bit version offers improved memory utilization, enhancing stability and performance for resource-intensive web applications.
VMWare ESX/i via API
We are happy to announce that the VMware ESX/i via API plugin now supports reconciliation using domain accounts. Until now, only local accounts could be used for reconciliation. This enhancement brings greater flexibility and simplifies privileged access management in domain-based environments
Plugin Generator Utility (PGU) enhanced browser support
To improve compatibility and greater flexibility for creating CPM and PSM plugins, we have expanded the browser support for Plugin Generator Utility (PGU), with the ability to generate plugins using Microsoft Edge in addition to Google Chrome.
We also automated the browser driver updates by integrating the WebDriverUpdater tool with PGU, removing the need for manual updates of Chrome or Edge drivers.
PSM WebApp infrastructure upgraded to 64-bit support
The PSM WebApp infrastructure now includes a 64-bit WebAppDispatcher. All components within the WebApp process are optimized for 64-bit architecture, offering improved performance and strengthened security.
In a clean PSM installation or in an upgrade, users get the new 64-bit dispatcher OOB. Any existing or new PSM OOB connection component built on the WebApp infrastructure automatically uses the 64-bit dispatcher. The 32-bit dispatcher is still available.
Connection components downloaded from CyberArk Marketplace are still in the 32-bit Connector folders. Users can configure PVWA to switch to the 64-bit dispatcher if needed.
The first downloaded connection component is saved in both locations.

HTML5 Gateway Docker deployment
This topic describes how to install the PSM HTML5 gateway via Docker.
Software prerequisites
Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.x versions with Docker
Install the HTML5 Gateway
This section describes how to install the PSM HTML5 Gateway as a docker.
-
Copy the HTML5 Gateway\PSMGWDocker directory located in the CD image to the Linux host.
-
Go to that directory.
-
Run the following command to grant execution rights to the setup script.
chmod +x html5_installation.sh
-
Run the following command to execute the setup script
sudo ./html5_installation.sh localimage
Launch the PSM HTML5 gateway Docker container
|
BY RUNNING PSM HTML5 GATEWAY DOCKER CONTAINER OR OTHERWISE USING THE SOFTWARE, YOU AGREE TO THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE SOFTWARE LICENSE AGREEMENT. IF YOU DO NOT AGREE TO THIS AGREEMENT, DO NOT INDICATE CONSENT ELECTRONICALLY AND MAKE NO FURTHER USE OF THE SOFTWARE. |
-
On the host machine, create a directory for certificates and related files. For example:
sudo mkdir /opt/cert
-
Place the following items in this directory to import them to the trusted store of the HTML5 Gateway docker:
- the .der or .pem certificate of the CA that signed the PSM certificate, or the PSM self-signed certificate
- the .der or .pem certificate of the CA that signed the PVWA certificate
These certificates are required because the Docker image is preconfigured to use TLS to establish a secure communication with certificate validation to PSM. Communication to PVWA as part of JWT validation also uses TLS with certificate validation.
-
If the PSM or JWT validation endpoints are signed by a CA chain, place all intermediate CA certificates in the mapped directory.
-
Using a self signed certificate is not recommended and should only be used for testing purposes.

Prepare a certificate for the PSM HTML5 gateway.
Use an existing certificate within your organization or create a new certificate.
Use an existing PSM HTML5 gateway certificate from your organizationPlace the following items in the directory you created in step 1:
-
Certificate to use as the PSM HTML5 gateway certificate, as a .crt file
-
Private key that matches the PSM HTML5 gateway remote certificate's public key, as a .key file
-
Certificate of the signing root CA, as a .crt file
If the certificate is signed by a CA chain and not just by a root CA, the CA certificate file must contain the entire chain and must be in PEM (Base64) format. To create the CA certificate file with the entire chain, concatenate the certificates into a combined file, starting from the inner CA with the root CA last.
Create a new PSM HTML5 gateway certificateYou can create a new certificate to use as the PSM HTML5 gateway's remote certificate.
-
Create a key file for the signing root CA:
sudo openssl genrsa -out <CA .key file output path> 4096
For example:
sudo openssl genrsa -out /opt/cert/rootCA.key 4096
Alternatively, to make the key password protected, add the -aes256 option:
sudo openssl genrsa -aes256 -out <CA .key file output path> 4096
For example:
sudo openssl genrsa -aes256 -out /opt/cert/rootCA.key 4096
Enter and verify the root CA private key password at the prompt.
- Create and self-sign the certificate for the root CA:
sudo openssl req -x509 -new -nodes -key <CA .key file path> -sha256 -days 1024 -out <CA .crt file output path>
For example:
sudo openssl req -x509 -new -nodes -key /opt/cert/rootCA.key -sha256 -days 1024 -out /opt/cert/rootCA.crt
-
At the prompt, enter any requested information.
If the root CA private key is password protected, you will be prompted for the password.The Common Name field is mandatory.
-
Create the PSM HTML5 gateway private key:
sudo openssl genrsa -out <Gateway .key file output path> 2048
For example:
sudo openssl genrsa -out /opt/cert/psmgw.key 2048
Alternatively, to make the key password protected, add the -aes256 option:
sudo openssl genrsa -aes256 -out <Gateway .key file output path> 2048
For example:
sudo openssl genrsa -aes256 -out /opt/cert/psmgw.key 2048
Enter and verify the PSM HTML5 gateway private key password at the prompt.
-
Create the certificate signing request for the PSM HTML5 gateway:
sudo openssl req -new -key <Gateway .key file path> -out <Gateway .csr file output path>
For example:
sudo openssl req -new -key /opt/cert/psmgw.key -out /opt/cert/psmgw.csr
-
At the prompt, enter any requested information.
If the PSM HTML5 gateway private key is password protected, you will be prompted for the password.The Common Name field is mandatory and its value must be different from the one created for the root CA certificate earlier.
-
Generate the HTML gateway certificate:
sudo openssl x509 -req -in <Gateway .csr file output path> -CA <CA .crt file path> -CAKey <CA .key file path> -CAcreateserial -out <Gateway .crt file output path> -days 1024 -sha256
For example:
sudo openssl x509 -req -in /opt/cert/psmgw.csr -CA /opt/cert/rootCA.crt -CAkey /opt/cert/rootCA.key -CAcreateserial -out /opt/cert/psmgw.crt -days 1024 -sha256
If the root CA private key is password protected, enter the password when prompted.

and replace <version_tag> with the value under TAG. -

Post-installation configuration
After installation, configure the HTML5 Gateway. For details, see Secure Access with an HTML5 Gateway.
Load balancing
The PSM HTML5 gateway can be load balanced as you would load balance any other web server (or the PVWA).
You can deploy farms of HTML5 gateway servers behind a load balancer. Then when adding a configured PSM Gateway server, use the relevant farm's Virtual IP (VIP) in the Address parameter. For details, see Add PSM HTML5 Gateway server.
In deployments where multiple connectors point to the same load-balanced URL, and multiple HTML5 gateways are behind this URL, the HTML5 copy files capability works if the Load Balancer has been configured with sticky sessions so that all requests for a particular user session are routed through the same HTML5 gateway.
You can perform a health check on the servers. For details, see Health Check.
Upgrade the PSM HTML5 Gateway
To upgrade the PSM HTML5 gateway, do the following:
-
Stop the running PSM HTML5 gateway container:
sudo docker kill <container name>
For example:
sudo docker kill <PSM gateway FQDN>
-
Delete the PSM HTML5 gateway container from the local Docker system:
sudo docker rm <container name>
For example:
sudo docker rm <PSM gateway FQDN>
-
Install the PSM HTML5 Gateway from the latest image, as described in Install the HTML5 Gateway.

Automate with the SCA provider for Terraform
This topic describes how to use the SCA provider for Terraform to automate the process of discovering updates to cloud workspaces that have been onboarded to CyberArk, and creating access policies for the identities that need to access these workspaces.
This topic is relevant if your access policies are managed in SCA's Policies page, or using the SCA Policies API.
If your access policies are managed in the Administration space or using the Access control policies API, see Automate with the Identity Security (idsec) Terraform provider.
If you are not sure where your policies are managed, contact CyberArk Support.
Migrated CyberArk tenants: If, before the migration, your organization was using the SCA Terraform Provider (described in this topic) to automate Secure Cloud Access operations, the automation will continue to work in the migrated tenant, but no more enhancements will be added. In addition, you need to make sure that all your policies have unique names.
Recommended: To take full advantage of ongoing support and future improvements for automation with Terraform, we strongly recommend redefining your automation using the unified idsec Terraform provider. For details, see Automate with the Identity Security (idsec) Terraform provider.
Overview
Cloud environments are dynamic, and many organizations add new workspaces on a regular basis.
If you already use Terraform to discover new workspaces in your cloud environment, you can integrate SCA discovery into your existing automation. This ensures that whenever new workspaces are added, an SCA policy is automatically applied to enforce the zero standing privilege model.
SCA supports using automation to add workspaces to organizations and directories that were previously onboarded to CyberArk.
Perform the procedures described in this topic for both first-time integrations and upgrades.

Step 2: Apply the CyberArk and cloud provider information
Specify the cloud identities and cloud provider information in your Terraform deployment to enable SCA to automate discovery and policy creation. Define the parameters in the variables.tf file, which are used by the main.tf file when it is run.
The SCA-Terraform template version is available in the main.tf file.
The variables.tf file contains the variables described in the subsections below.
sca_provider
The parameters in the sca_provider
section are required for any automation that you want to configure.
|
Variable |
Description |
|---|---|
|
auth_url |
OAuth2 URL for authenticating from CyberArk Identity |
|
tenant_domain_name |
The tenant subdomain, which is the same as tenant_name in the SCA REST API, for example, see SCA infrastructure APIs. For example, if your tenant URL is abc1234.cyberark.cloud, then specify abc1234. If you downloaded the Terraform template files before 16 October 2024, the value of tenant_domain_name must be in the format <tenant_name>-sca. For example, if your tenant URL is abc1234.cyberark.cloud, then specify |
|
platform_domain_name |
The platform domain Default: cyberark.cloud |
|
username |
SCA service user username for the API |
|
password |
Password used by the SCA service user for the API |
|
debug |
Use this parameter to turn debug mode on or off for the resources and data source Default: false |
Example
In this example of the sca_provider
section in the main.tf file, the tenant URL is example.cyberark.cloud
.
provider "sca" {
auth_url = "https://{identity_tenant}.id.cyberark.cloud/oauth2/token/{webapp}"
tenant_domain_name = "abc1234"
platform_domain_name = "cyberark.cloud"
username = "service_username@cyberark.cloud.xxx"
password = "service_username_password"
debug = true
}
sca_discovery
The variables in the sca_discovery
data section are used to automate discovering new workspaces or roles. If you don't want to automate this activity, you can delete the section in the variables.tf file.
|
Variable |
Description |
|---|---|
|
csp |
Cloud service provider Supported values:
|
|
organization_id |
Root organization ID for the cloud provider workspace to which the policy applies |
|
account_info |
A dictionary with the following parameters:
|
Example
In this example, the AWS account 11111111, which belongs to the r-xxx organization, is new and is being discovered.
The sca_discovery section in the main.tf file looks as follows:
data "sca_discovery" "discovery_example" {
csp = "AWS
organization_id = "r-xxxx"
account_info = {
id = "1111111111"
new_account = false
sca_policy
The variables in the sca_policy
section are used to create SCA policies. If you don't want to automate this activity, you can delete the section in the variables.tf file.
|
Variable |
Description |
|---|---|
|
name |
The name of the policy. |
|
description |
The description of the policy. |
|
csp |
Cloud service provider Supported values:
|
|
roles |
Cloud provider roles to which the policy applies, defined by the following: |
|
entity_id
|
|
|
entity_source_id
|
|
|
organization_id
|
|
|
|
workspace_type
|
|
identities |
Identities (users) to which the policy applies, defined by the following:
|
|
start_date |
(Optional) The date and time when the policy becomes active, in ISO format. |
|
end_date |
(Optional) The date and time when the policy expires, in ISO format. |
|
access_rules |
A set of rules that specify when the policy is active.
|
Example
See this example of the sca_policy section in the main.tf file.
resource "sca_policy" "policy_example" {
csp = "AWS"
roles = [
{
entity_id = "arn:aws:iam::xxxxxxxxxxxx:role/devOps"
entity_source_id = "xxxxxxxxxxxx"
workspace_type = "account"
}
]
identities = [
{
entity_name = "user@cyberark.cloud.xxx"
entity_source_id = "id"
entity_class = "user"
}
]
access_rules = {
days = [
"sunday",
"monday",
"tuesday",
"wednesday",
"thursday",
"friday",
"saturday"
]
from_time = "09:00"
to_time = "17:00"
max_session_duration = 1
time_zone = "Asia/Jerusalem"
}
start_date = "2022-07-12T00:00:00.000Z"
end_date = "2022-10-10T00:00:00.000Z"
}
sca_queryPolicies
The variables in the sca_queryPolicies data
section are used to query the status of a policy during automation operations. If you don't want to automate this activity, you can delete the section in the variables.tf file.
|
Variable |
Description |
|---|---|
|
csp |
Cloud service provider Supported values:
|
|
status |
Filter policies according to status Supported values:
|
|
free_text |
Search using free text. The following parameters are supported:
|
|
page_size |
Define the number of results that should appear per page (maximum = 100) |
Example
data "sca_queryPolicies" "queryPolicies_example" {
free_text = "PolicyForITTeam"
csp = "AWS"
status = "Active"
page_size = 50
}

Run the following commands from the main.tf file:
terraform init
terraform apply
To run Terraform in debug mode, use the following command:
TF_LOG=DEBUG terraform apply

This topic describes how to add a web app for Microsoft Entra ID (previously Azure AD) to enable access from CyberArk Identity.
Before you begin
The sections below assume that:
-
If you are working with an external IdP, your organization's users have already been provisioned to CyberArk Identity such that your users exist in both the external IdP and in CyberArk. For details, see Add Microsoft Entra ID as a directory service.
In addition, check if there is an app registration in Azure for the identity provider. If not, you will be able to create one in this flow.
-
Microsoft Entra ID has already been onboarded to CyberArk. If you haven't yet onboarded Microsoft Entra ID, do so before you add the web app. For details, see Add Azure Microsoft Entra ID (Cloud Visibility).
Step 1: Create a web app in Identity Administration
Start by creating the actual web app for Microsoft Entra ID in the platform.
You can create web apps in one of the following ways:
|
Option |
Description |
|---|---|
|
SCA (simplified) |
In SCA, you provide a few details about Microsoft Entra ID, and the web app is automatically created and configured for you. Depending on your selections during this process, you may need to configure a few more things. |
|
Identity Administration |
In Identity Administration, you create and configure the web app from scratch. |
-
-
In SCA, go to the Introduction page.
-
In the second tile, click + Create a web app.
-
In the dialog box that opens click Azure, and click Next.

Enter a name for the web app (up to 50 characters) that will help you identify it in CyberArk Identity.

Select the Microsoft Entra ID directory.

-
If your Microsoft Entra ID doesn't appear, this means that it hasn't yet been onboarded to CyberArk. For details about onboarding Microsoft Entra ID, see Onboard a new directory.
-
-
Click Create.
This triggers an asynchronous discovery of your onboarded workspaces to identify changes in your cloud structure. This may take some time. We recommend that you wait for this process to complete before creating policies in SCA.

-
Sign in to Identity Administration.
-
Under Apps & Widgets, select Web Apps, and click Add Web Apps.

In the Search tab, search for Azure.

Next to the Microsoft Azure Portal: WS-FED+Provisioning web app, click Add, and click Yes to confirm.

Permissions

-
Group.ReadWrite.All

-
User.ReadWrite.All

Azure application setting
Value

Terraform
Install Terraform
Terraform lets you safely and consistently manage your infrastructure as code across multiple cloud providers. To provision infrastructure with Terraform, you will write configuration in Terraform's configuration language, configure your cloud provider credentials, and apply your configuration with the Terraform Command Line Interface (CLI).
To use Terraform, you first need to install it. HashiCorp distributes Terraform as a binary package. You can also install Terraform using popular package managers.
Install Terraform
HashiCorp distributes Terraform as an executable CLI that you can install on supported operating systems, including Microsoft Windows, macOS, and several Linux distributions. You can also compile the Terraform CLI from source if a pre-compiled binary is not available for your system.
If you use a package manager to install software on your macOS, Windows, or Linux system, you can use it to install Terraform.
Homebrew is a free and open-source package management system for macOS. If you have Homebrew installed, use it to install Terraform from your command line.
First, install the HashiCorp tap, which is Hashicorp's official repository of all our Homebrew packages.
$ brew tap hashicorp/tap
Now, install Terraform from hashicorp/tap/terraform
.
$ brew install hashicorp/tap/terraform
Terraform versions and compatibility
HashiCorp regularly releases new versions of Terraform with new features and bug fixes. HashiCorp maintains compatibility between Terraform versions, so a Terraform configuration written for one version of Terraform should continue to work with any later minor version update. Refer to the Terraform compatibility promise for more details.
Verify the Installation
Verify that the installation worked by opening a new terminal session and listing Terraform's available subcommands.
$ terraform -help
Usage: terraform [global options] <subcommand> [args]
The available commands for execution are listed below.
The primary workflow commands are given first, followed by

If you use either Bash or Zsh as your command line shell, you can enable tab completion for Terraform commands. To enable autocomplete, first ensure that a configuration file exists for your chosen shell.

Create a web app for AWS
This topic describes how to add web apps for single AWS IAM accounts, AWS IAM organizations, and AWS IAM Identity Center organizations to enable access from CyberArk Identity.
This topic assumes that your AWS workspace has been onboarded to CyberArk. For details, see Add AWS (Cloud Visibility).
Special considerations for AWS IAM Identity Center
If you are creating one or more web apps for AWS IAM Identity Center, take the following issues into consideration when planning which IdP to use with the CyberArk Identity web apps.
-
Active Directory: If you intend to switch your IdP to or from Active Directory, this will affect any users and groups you configured in AWS. For more information, see the AWS docs.
-
Permission set behavior: SCA enforces zero standing permissions, which involves dynamically assigning and revoking permissions to the AWS cloud console. This might directly affect AWS reserved roles (AWSReserved roles), which are dynamically managed by AWS behind the scenes.
If you have an IAM policy or a resource-based policy—such as one linked to an Amazon EKS cluster—that explicitly references an AWSReservedSSO role ARN, this configuration may be impacted. For more information, see the AWS docs. To prevent disruptions, each account must have at least one permanent assignment to the permission set. Contact CyberArk Support to enable a feature flag that preserves the roles.
